about: codelaw's rule catalogue, generated by scripts/rule-docs.py from the rule files. `title` states the rule as what the code does; `dont` and `do` are the first line of the example's don't and do that the other lacks (null when there is none, as for a deletion); `example` is the first language's full don't and do

rules.title: A DAG names its schedule
rules.fix_reason: the schedule is the author's
fix_steps: Add `schedule=` with a cron string, a timetable or `None`.

example.dont:
from airflow import DAG
with DAG(dag_id='etl', start_date=start):
    pass
example.do:
from airflow import DAG
with DAG(dag_id='etl', start_date=start, schedule='@daily'):
    pass

rules.title: Variable.get inside a task
rules.fix_reason: moving the read into the task or a template changes the DAG's code
fix_steps: Move the call into the task function, or use the `{{ var.value.name }}` template.

example.dont:
from airflow.models import Variable
bucket = Variable.get('bucket')

rules.title: A task's variable is named like its task_id
rules.fix_reason: the `task_id` changes, which renames the task in the UI and its history

example.dont:
from airflow.operators.python import PythonOperator
load = PythonOperator(task_id="extract", python_callable=run)
example.do:
from airflow.operators.python import PythonOperator
load = PythonOperator(task_id="load", python_callable=run)

rules.title: task.output, not xcom_pull in a template
rules.fix_reason: the operator's argument becomes a reference to the upstream task
fix_steps: Pass `upstream_task.output` (or `upstream_task.output['key']`) as the argument.

example.dont:
from airflow.operators.bash import BashOperator
BashOperator(task_id='b', bash_command="echo {{ ti.xcom_pull(task_ids='a') }}")
example.do:
from airflow.operators.bash import BashOperator
BashOperator(task_id='b', bash_command=a.output)

rules.title: No changing values in a DAG's arguments
rules.fix_reason: the fixed value is the author's
fix_steps: Use a fixed date, for example `pendulum.datetime(2026, 1, 1, tz='UTC')`.

example.dont:
from airflow import DAG
from datetime import datetime
with DAG(dag_id='etl', start_date=datetime.now(), schedule='@daily'):
    pass
example.do:
from airflow import DAG
from datetime import datetime
with DAG(dag_id='etl', start_date=datetime(2026, 1, 1), schedule='@daily'):
    pass

rules.title: CSS Module class names can be read as styles.name
rules.fix_reason: renaming a class must update every file that reads it

style.description: `camelCase` (a name `styles.x` reaches without brackets), `kebab` (kebab-case) or `any` (no check)

fix_steps: Rename the class (and every `styles.…` that reads it) to camelCase.
Or set `[css] modules_convention = "camelCase"` if the bundler already maps the names.

rules.title: composes points at a class that exists
rules.fix_reason: which class to compose is the author's call
fix_steps: Correct the class name or the path.
Move `composes` into the rule whose selector is the one class that composes.

rules.title: A CSS Module stays local
rules.fix_reason: a global selector exists to reach markup outside the module, which is the author's call
fix_steps: Move the rule into a plain `.css` file, or give the markup a local class.

rules.title: A CSS Module class that is read exists
rules.fix_reason: whether to add the class or fix the name is the author's call
fix_steps: Correct the name in the JavaScript or TypeScript file, or add the class to the module.
If the bundler maps names (`localsConvention`), set `[css] modules_convention` so the mapped names count.

rules.title: A CSS Module class is read somewhere
rules.fix_reason: a class can be read by a name built at run time or by code outside the repo, so deleting its rule needs a person to accept the diff
fix_steps: Search for the class: `styles.name`, a bracket access, and any `composes` that names it.
If a component builds the name at run time, read it by a plain `styles.name` somewhere, or accept that this module is dynamic.
Otherwise delete the rule (`codelaw fix --unsafe` does it when the class is the rule's only selector).

rules.title: A stylesheet stays under a line limit
rules.fix_reason: splitting a stylesheet changes its structure and the order of the cascade

max.description: the most lines a stylesheet may have

skip_comments.description: comment-only lines do not count: `/* */` and, in SCSS, `//`

fix_steps: Split the stylesheet by component or by concern: one file per component, or `base`, `layout`, `components`, `utilities`.
In SCSS, move each part to a partial (`_buttons.scss`) and pull it in with `@use`; with CSS Modules, one module per component.
Keep the order the cascade needs: import the parts in the order they had in the original file.
If the limit is wrong for these files, raise it for them with a `[scope]` table rather than for the project.

rules.title: No line breaks inside selector strings
rules.fix_reason: whether the line break was meant is the author's call
fix_steps: Join the string onto one line, or escape the line break as `\A`.

rules.title: `@property` syntax strings are valid
rules.fix_reason: the intended type is the author's call
fix_steps: Use a supported type name such as `<length>`, `<color>` or `<number>`.

rules.title: No transition or animation too short to see
rules.fix_reason: the duration is the author's to choose

min.description: the shortest duration allowed, in milliseconds

fix_steps: Lengthen the duration, or remove the transition.

rules.title: CSS TODO comments carry a ticket and, when asked, a date
rules.fix_reason: a ticket and a date are facts about the work that only the author knows; the engine can't invent them
fix_steps: Open or find the ticket for the work and write it in the parentheses: `TODO(ABC-123): …`.
When the project asks for a date (`require_date`), or the work has a deadline, add it: `TODO(ABC-123, 2027-01-31): …`.
For an expired marker: do the work and delete the comment; or, if the work really moves, change the date and say why in the text.
If the comment is not a to-do, rewrite it so it does not open with the tag.

example.dont:
/* FIXME: remove after the redesign */
.legacy { margin: 0; }
example.do:
/* FIXME(UI-12): remove after the redesign */
.legacy { margin: 0; }

rules.title: Only units the project allows
rules.fix_reason: what the project uses instead of the unit is its own convention, which the code doesn't hold

list.description: the units allowed (`/re/` for a regular expression)

fix_steps: Use an allowed unit, or change the list.

rules.title: No unit the project disallows
rules.fix_reason: what the project uses instead of the unit is its own convention, which the code doesn't hold

list.description: the units disallowed (`/re/` for a regular expression)

fix_steps: Use an other unit, or change the list.

rules.title: Flow-relative units, not physical ones
rules.fix_reason: a flow-relative unit follows the writing mode, so in a vertical layout it measures the other axis
fix_steps: Use the flow-relative unit.

rules.title: No unknown units
rules.fix_reason: which unit was meant is the author's to say
fix_steps: Fix the unit.

rules.title: Flow-relative keywords, not physical ones
rules.fix_reason: a flow-relative keyword follows the writing mode, so in a right-to-left layout it lands on the other side
fix_steps: Use the flow-relative keyword.

rules.title: No vendor-prefixed values
rules.fix_reason: browsers that need the prefix lose the value

ignoreValues.description: values to accept, without their prefix; `/regex/` for a pattern

rules.title: Every file has a code owner, and every CODEOWNERS pattern is live
rules.fix_reason: who owns a path is a decision about people; the finding names the paths and the lines, and the owner is the team's to choose

path.description: the CODEOWNERS file, from the project root; by default the first that exists of .github/CODEOWNERS, CODEOWNERS, docs/CODEOWNERS and .gitlab/CODEOWNERS

allow_unowned.description: a pattern that names no owner is meant: it is not reported, and neither are its paths

ignore.description: gitignore-style patterns of paths that need no owner, such as *.lock

fix_steps: For an unowned path, add a pattern that covers it to the CODEOWNERS file (`/src/payments/ @org/payments`), or a catch-all `* @org/maintainers` first so every later pattern refines it.
For a stale pattern, delete the line, or correct the pattern to the folder or file it now means.
For a pattern with no owner, name one — or, if the path is meant to have none, set `[codeowners] allow_unowned = true`.
For paths that never need a review (lockfiles, generated files), list them in `[codeowners] ignore`.

rules.title: The feature-flag registry is valid and holds only flags still read

presets.description: `[flags] presets`, for this rule only: the SDKs whose reads codelaw knows (launchdarkly, unleash, split, openfeature, growthbook, flagsmith)

accessors.description: `[flags] accessors`, for this rule only: calls with one `$NAME` slot that read a flag

inline.description: `[flags] inline`, for this rule only: `allow` or `registry-only`

warn_days.description: `[flags] warn_days`, for this rule only: how many days before `expires` a read warns

fix_steps: Run `codelaw fix`: an entry with no read left is removed.
Otherwise edit the entry: give it a `name`, an `expires` date (or `never` and a `reason`), `keep = "on"` or `"off"` only, and no other keys.

example.dont:
# .codelaw/flags.toml
[[flag]]
name = "new-checkout"
owner = "@payments"
expires = "2027-02-28"

[[flag]]
name = "old-banner"
owner = "@web"
expires = "2026-06-30"
# src/checkout.js
export const on = isFeatureOn("new-checkout");
example.do:
# .codelaw/flags.toml
[[flag]]
name = "new-checkout"
owner = "@payments"
expires = "2027-02-28"
# src/checkout.js
export const on = isFeatureOn("new-checkout");

rules.title: Every advisory source was read
rules.fix_reason: reading an advisory source again needs the network, which the engine never uses (L5); turning a source off is the team's decision
fix_steps: Run `codelaw deps refresh` once the source is reachable, and commit the snapshot.
If the organisation will never allow that source, set `enabled = false` on it in `[deps] advisory_sources`, so the scan is complete as configured.

rules.title: Every dependency has a licence the project allows
rules.fix_reason: replacing a package, or accepting its licence, is a legal and product decision no tool can make
fix_steps: Read the package's licence. If the project can accept it, add its id to `[deps.licence] allow`.
Otherwise replace the package (or the dependency that brings it in), then run the install.
For a known exception, add a dated `[deps.licence] ignore` entry with `reason` and `added_by`.

rules.title: The lockfile matches its manifest
rules.fix_reason: only the package manager can write its lockfile, and codelaw never runs installers
fix_steps: Run the command the message names in the folder of the lockfile.
Commit the manifest and the lockfile together.

rules.title: Dependencies are on their latest version
rules.fix_reason: a new major or minor version can change behaviour; the fix moves the range to the latest version, and the code that uses the package may need changes
fix_steps: Run `codelaw fix --unsafe` to move the range to the latest version, or edit the version by hand.
Run your package manager's install (`npm install`, `uv lock`, …) so the lockfile follows.
For a major version, read the package's changelog and update the code that uses it.
If the project must stay on this version, add the package to `[deps] ignore`, with an `expires` date when the stay is temporary.

rules.title: Every place that names the Node or Python version agrees
rules.fix_reason: changing a runtime pin changes what CI, the container or a developer's shell runs; the agreed version may not be the one the team meant
fix_steps: Run `codelaw fix --unsafe` to move the pins in `package.json`, `mise.toml` and the workflows to the agreed version.
Edit the version files and the `Dockerfile`'s `FROM` line to the same version by hand.
If the range is what is wrong, widen `engines.node` or `requires-python`.

rules.title: The dependency snapshot is recent
rules.fix_reason: refreshing the snapshot reads the registries, which needs the network; the engine never uses it (L5)
fix_steps: Run `codelaw deps refresh`: it reads npm and the Python index and writes the snapshot again.
Commit `.codelaw/deps-snapshot.json`, so CI and every teammate judge by the same facts.

rules.title: A monorepo declares each dependency with one range
rules.fix_reason: aligning a range changes what that workspace installs; the lower range may be on purpose
fix_steps: Run `codelaw fix --unsafe` to align the range, or edit it by hand.
Run the install so the lockfile follows.
If a workspace needs another version on purpose, add the package to `[deps.drift] ignore`.

rules.title: No dependency in use has a known vulnerability
rules.fix_reason: the fix moves a range or adds an override to the lowest known-clean version, which changes what installs; a new major can change behaviour, and an override changes the install of the whole tree
fix_steps: Run `codelaw fix --unsafe` to move the range (or add the override) to the version named, or make the same edit by hand.
Run the install the message names (`npm install`, `pnpm install`, `yarn install`, `uv lock`, `poetry lock`) so the lockfile follows; codelaw never runs installers.
For a new major, read the package's changelog and update the code that uses it.
With no clean version: replace the package, remove it, or add a dated `[deps] ignore` entry naming the advisory, with a reason.

rules.title: ModelForm does not use fields = '__all__'
rules.fix_reason: the fields to list are the author's
fix_steps: Set `fields` to the list of fields the form shows.

rules.title: ModelForm lists fields, not exclude
rules.fix_reason: the fields to list are the author's
fix_steps: Replace `exclude` with `fields = [...]` naming each field the form shows.

rules.title: No locals() as a template context
rules.fix_reason: the context's keys are the author's to list
fix_steps: Pass a dict of the names the template uses.

rules.title: A model defines __str__
rules.fix_reason: what represents the object is the author's to choose
fix_steps: Add `def __str__(self): return self.<name field>`.

rules.title: @receiver is the first decorator
rules.fix_reason: reordering decorators changes which wrapper is connected
fix_steps: Move `@receiver(...)` to the top of the decorator list.

rules.title: No null=True on string fields
rules.fix_reason: removing `null=True` needs a migration and a default for the existing NULLs
fix_steps: Remove `null=True` (keep `blank=True` if the field is optional) and migrate existing NULLs to `''`.

rules.title: A model's body follows Django's order
rules.fix_reason: moving members reorders the class by hand
fix_steps: Move the fields to the top of the class and `class Meta` after them, before any method.

rules.title: Dependencies through Annotated
rules.fix_reason: the suggestion uses `Annotated`, which the file must import from `typing`

example.dont:
async def read(db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    return db
example.do:
async def read(db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)]):
    return db

rules.title: No response_model that repeats the return annotation
CSS classes must be used somewhere
rules.fix_reason: A class can be built at run time or used by markup outside the repo, so removing its rule needs a human or agent to accept the diff.
fix_steps: Search for the class: a name built at run time (`"btn-" + kind`) counts only through its static prefix.
If markup outside the repo uses it, add the file to `[graph] keep` or list it in the package's `style` or `exports`.
Otherwise delete the rule, or the class from its selector list.

rules.title: Exported symbols must be used somewhere
rules.fix_reason: Static analysis can't rule out reflective or external use, so removal needs a human or agent to accept the diff.
rules.dont: export function parseDate(s) { return new Date(s); }
fix_steps: Run `codelaw graph why-unused <symbol>` (`<file>#<export>` or `<module>:<name>`) to see each entry, keep and import clause.
If something outside the repo uses it, add the file to `[graph] entry` or `[graph] keep`, add its decorator to `[graph] registrars`, or tag it `/** @public */` / `# codelaw: keep`.
Otherwise delete the declaration (and its `__all__` or `export { … }` entry), or drop `export` if its own file still uses it.

rules.title: Only the kinds of link the project allows
rules.fix_reason: which address to link to is the author's to write
fix_steps: Rewrite the address in an allowed form.

rules.title: Image-map areas with a link have alt text
rules.fix_reason: the text that describes the area needs a human

accessible.description: require `alt` on every linked area, not just one area per link target

fix_steps: Give each linked `<area>` an `alt` that says where it leads.
Remove `alt` from an `<area>` that has no `href`.

rules.title: <body> is not aria-hidden
rules.fix_reason: removing it exposes the page to screen readers again, which changes what users hear

rules.title: aria-label is used only where it names something
rules.fix_reason: whether to move the label, add a role or use another element is a design decision

allowAnyNamable.description: accept the label on any element ARIA lets be named, even where support is poor

fix_steps: If the element acts as a control, use the matching element (`<button>`, `<a href>`) or add a `role`.
Otherwise put the text in the content, where everyone can read it, and remove the attribute.

rules.title: Attribute names follow the project's pattern
rules.fix_reason: renaming the attribute must also change what reads it

pattern.description: a regular expression attribute names must match

fix_steps: Rename the attribute.

rules.title: Attributes have values HTML allows
rules.fix_reason: the intended value can only be guessed
fix_steps: Check the attribute's allowed values (the message lists the one written).
Correct the value, or remove the attribute to get the default.

rules.title: Attributes are used only where they take effect
rules.fix_reason: either the attribute or its context is wrong, and only the author knows which
fix_steps: Read the message: it names the attribute and what it needs.
Add the missing context (for example `href` or `type="submit"`), or remove the attribute.

rules.title: Password fields say which password they want
rules.fix_reason: whether the field asks for a new or the current password depends on the form

preferred.description: one value every password field must use, such as `current-password`

fix_steps: Use `autocomplete="current-password"` on a sign-in form.
Use `autocomplete="new-password"` on a sign-up or change-password form.

rules.title: <button> says what type it is
rules.fix_reason: `type="button"` stops the button submitting its form; a button meant to submit needs `type="submit"` instead

rules.title: Class names follow the project's pattern
rules.fix_reason: renaming the class must also change the stylesheets and scripts that use it

pattern.description: a regular expression class names must match

fix_steps: Rename the class, and its uses in CSS and scripts.

rules.title: Elements are closed, and in the order they were opened
rules.fix_reason: where the missing end tag belongs depends on the intended structure
fix_steps: Find where the element named in the message should end.
Add its end tag there, or remove an end tag that closes nothing.

rules.title: No obsolete elements
rules.fix_reason: the replacement — CSS, a semantic element, or nothing — depends on the intent
fix_steps: Read the message for the usual replacement.
Use that element, or a class and CSS, instead.

rules.title: No class the project has deprecated
rules.fix_reason: auto when the option gives the class's `replacement`; a class with only a message is reported without an edit

classes.description: deprecated class → its replacement (empty for none)

rules.title: The doctype is the HTML5 one
rules.fix_reason: switching to standards mode can change the page's layout

rules.title: Element names are HTML elements or valid custom elements
rules.fix_reason: renaming an element changes its CSS and script hooks
fix_steps: If the name is a typo of an HTML element, correct it.
If it is a custom element, give it a hyphenated name and rename its definition.
If a framework needs the name, add it to the `allow` option.

rules.title: Elements contain only content HTML allows there
rules.fix_reason: the right structure depends on what the markup is for
fix_steps: Move the element named in the message out of the parent it can't be in.
Or change the parent to one that allows it (for example `<div>` instead of `<span>`).

rules.title: Elements that may appear once do
rules.fix_reason: which of the duplicates to keep is the author's call
fix_steps: Merge the duplicates into one, or remove the extra one.

rules.title: Children come in the order HTML requires
rules.fix_reason: moving markup may change how it is styled
fix_steps: Move the element named in the message before the one it must precede.

rules.title: Elements have a parent HTML allows
rules.fix_reason: whether to wrap the element or change it depends on the intended structure
fix_steps: Wrap the element in the parent it needs.
Or replace it with an element that fits where it is.

rules.title: Elements are inside the ancestor they need
rules.fix_reason: whether to add the ancestor or use other elements depends on the intent
fix_steps: Wrap the elements in the ancestor the message names.
Or replace them with elements that make sense where they are.

rules.title: Elements have the attributes HTML requires
rules.fix_reason: the value can only come from the author
fix_steps: Add the attribute the message names, with the right value.

rules.title: Elements contain the children HTML requires
rules.fix_reason: the content of the missing child needs a human
fix_steps: Add the child the message names, with real content.

rules.title: Headings have text
rules.fix_reason: the heading text needs a human
fix_steps: Give the heading text, or remove it if it only made space (use CSS for that).

rules.title: <title> has text
rules.fix_reason: the page title needs a human
fix_steps: Write a short title that says what the page is.

rules.title: <fieldset> has a legend
rules.fix_reason: the group's name needs a human
fix_steps: Add a `<legend>` as the fieldset's first child, naming the group.

rules.title: Form controls have unique names
rules.fix_reason: renaming a control changes what the server receives

allowCheckboxDefault.description: allow a hidden input before a checkbox of the same name

shared.description: control types that may share a name

fix_steps: Give each control its own name, and update the code that reads the form.

rules.title: Forms have a submit button
rules.fix_reason: the button's label and placement need a human
fix_steps: Add a `<button type="submit">` with a label that says what it does.

rules.title: Headings start at <h1> and go down one level at a time
rules.fix_reason: changing a heading level changes its style and the outline

minInitialRank.description: the lowest level the first heading may have (`h1`–`h6`, or `any`)

sectioningRoots.description: selectors of elements that start their own outline

fix_steps: Change the heading to the level the message expects, and restyle it with CSS if it looked right before.

rules.title: Focusable elements are not aria-hidden
rules.fix_reason: whether to unhide it, take it out of the tab order or remove it depends on the design
fix_steps: Remove `aria-hidden` if the element should be announced.
Otherwise take it out of the tab order with `tabindex="-1"`, or hide it from everyone with `hidden` or `inert`.

rules.title: Ids follow the project's pattern
rules.fix_reason: renaming the id must also change the links, labels, styles and scripts that use it

pattern.description: a regular expression ids must match

fix_steps: Rename the id and its references.

rules.title: has alt text
rules.fix_reason: only a human can describe the image, or decide it is decorative

alias.description: other attributes that count as alt text, such as a framework binding

fix_steps: Describe what the image shows, or what it is for, in `alt`.
If the image is decorative, write `alt=""`.

rules.title: Decorative images have no title
rules.fix_reason: whether the image is decorative or informative is the author's call
fix_steps: If the image carries information, move the text from `title` to `alt`.
If it is decorative, remove the `title`.

rules.title: Input attributes fit the input type
rules.fix_reason: scripts or attribute selectors may still read the attribute

rules.title: Image buttons have alt text
rules.fix_reason: the text needs a human
fix_steps: Add `alt` saying what the button does.

rules.title: Form controls have a label
rules.fix_reason: the label text needs a human
fix_steps: Add a `<label for>` with text, or wrap the control in a `<label>`.
If a visible label is impossible, add `aria-label`.

rules.title: Links have text
rules.fix_reason: the link text needs a human
fix_steps: Give the link text, an image with `alt`, or an `aria-label`.

rules.title: Page titles are short
rules.fix_reason: shortening a title needs a human

maxlength.description: the longest title allowed, in characters

rules.dont: <title>Acme Corporation — Products, Services, Pricing, Support, Downloads and Contact Details</title>
fix_steps: Shorten the title to what identifies the page.

example.dont: <title>Acme Corporation — Products, Services, Pricing, Support, Downloads and Contact Details</title>

rules.title: Image maps have unique names
rules.fix_reason: renaming a map means updating the `usemap` that points at it
fix_steps: Rename one map and the `usemap` attributes that refer to it.

rules.title: A map's id and name match
rules.fix_reason: which of the two names is right depends on what refers to the map
fix_steps: Make `id` and `name` equal, and update references to the one you changed.

rules.title: A page stays under a line limit
rules.fix_reason: splitting a page into partials or components changes its structure

max.description: the most lines a page or template may have

skip_embedded.description: lines inside `<script>` and `<style>` do not count (the JS and CSS rules check their content)

fix_steps: Pull a self-contained part (header, footer, a card, a form) into a partial, include or component.
Move a large inline `<script>` or `<style>` into its own file and link it.
If the limit is wrong for these files, raise it for them with a `[scope]` table rather than for the project.

rules.title: Meta refresh redirects at once
rules.fix_reason: redirecting at once or removing the refresh changes the page's behaviour
fix_steps: Make the refresh instant with `0;url=…`.
Or replace it with a link the user follows when ready.

rules.title: The document has a doctype
rules.fix_reason: leaving quirks mode can change the page's layout

rules.title: A label labels one control
rules.fix_reason: each control needs its own label text
fix_steps: Give each control its own `<label>`.

example.do:
<label>First name <input type="text" name="first"></label>
<label>Last name <input type="text" name="last"></label>

rules.title: Form field names follow the project's pattern
rules.fix_reason: renaming a form field changes what the server receives

pattern.description: a regular expression form field names must match

fix_steps: Rename the field, here and where the form is read.

rules.title: No abstract ARIA roles
rules.fix_reason: the concrete role depends on what the element is
fix_steps: Use the concrete role that describes the element, or a native element.

rules.title: Media does not play by itself
rules.fix_reason: the media no longer starts on load

rules.title: No Internet Explorer conditional comments
rules.fix_reason: whether the markup inside is still needed is the author's call
fix_steps: Delete the conditional comment, or move markup that is still needed out of it.

rules.title: No obsolete attributes
rules.fix_reason: the replacement is usually CSS, which needs a class and a rule
fix_steps: Replace presentational attributes with a class and CSS.
Replace other obsolete attributes with their current equivalent (for example `id` for `<a name>`).

rules.title: Ids are unique in the document
rules.fix_reason: renaming an id breaks the CSS, scripts and links that use it
fix_steps: Decide which element keeps the id.
Rename the other one, and update the CSS, scripts, `for`, `aria-*` and links that refer to it.

rules.title: Elements are closed explicitly
rules.fix_reason: the end tag goes after the element's last content, so whitespace that followed it moves outside the element

rules.title: <input> says what type it is
rules.fix_reason: `type="text"` is the default, but the field may have been meant as another type

rules.title: No inline event handlers or javascript: URLs
rules.fix_reason: the handler has to move into a script file
fix_steps: Give the element an id or class.
Attach the listener with `addEventListener` in a script file.
Replace a `javascript:` link with a `<button>`.

rules.title: No inline styles
rules.fix_reason: the styles need a class and a stylesheet rule

allowedProperties.description: properties an inline style may set

allowVariables.description: let inline styles set custom properties (`--name`)

fix_steps: Move the declarations into a stylesheet rule for a class.
Replace the `style` attribute with that class.

rules.title: Id references point at an element
rules.fix_reason: either the id or the reference is wrong, and only the author knows which
fix_steps: Correct the reference, or add the element it should point at.

example.do: Use your work address.

rules.title: One visible <main> per document
rules.fix_reason: which one is the main content is a design decision
fix_steps: Keep one `<main>`; make the others `<section>`, `<aside>` or similar, or hide inactive ones with `hidden`.

rules.title: A wrapping label has no for
No role the element already has
No `<style>` element
rules.fix_reason: moving styles into a stylesheet changes the files the page loads
fix_steps: Move the rules into a stylesheet and link it.

rules.title: No attribute the element doesn't have
rules.fix_reason: which attribute was meant is the author's to say
fix_steps: Fix the name, or use a `data-` attribute.

rules.title: No element HTML doesn't define
rules.fix_reason: which element was meant is the author's to say
fix_steps: Fix the name, or give a custom element a dashed name.

rules.title: No UTF-8 byte-order mark
rules.fix_reason: the mark is in the file's bytes, outside the text a fix can edit; the editor's encoding setting removes it
fix_steps: Save the file as UTF-8 without a byte-order mark. In VS Code, click the encoding in the status bar, choose *Save with Encoding*, then *UTF-8*.
Or strip it from the command line: `sed -i '1s/^\xEF\xBB\xBF//' <file>` (GNU sed).

rules.title: Buttons are <button> elements
rules.fix_reason: the element changes, so CSS and scripts that select `input` need updating
fix_steps: Replace the `<input>` with a `<button>` of the same type, moving `value` into the content.
Update the CSS selectors and scripts that targeted the input.

rules.title: Native elements instead of ARIA roles
rules.fix_reason: swapping the element changes its styles and scripts
fix_steps: Replace the element with the native one the message names.
Remove the `role` and any keyboard handling the native element now provides.

rules.title: Inline scripts and styles carry a nonce
rules.fix_reason: the nonce comes from the server for each response
fix_steps: Have the server put the response's nonce on the element.

rules.title: Scripts and stylesheets carry an integrity hash
rules.fix_reason: the hash must be computed from the exact file served

target.description: `all` checks every resource; `crossorigin` only those loaded from another origin

fix_steps: Compute the file's hash, for example `openssl dgst -sha384 -binary lib.js | openssl base64 -A`.
Add `integrity="sha384-…"` and `crossorigin="anonymous"`.

rules.title: <script> has an end tag
rules.fix_reason: the markup the open script swallowed starts being rendered

rules.title: Links that open a new tab set rel="noopener"
Phone numbers don't wrap
rules.fix_reason: the text then contains non-breaking characters, which copy and search keep

rules.title: Buttons have text
rules.fix_reason: the button's name needs a human
fix_steps: Add visible text, or an `aria-label` that says what the button does.

rules.title: Header cells in complex tables have scope
rules.fix_reason: whether each header labels a row or a column is the author's call
fix_steps: Add `scope="col"` to column headers and `scope="row"` to row headers.

rules.title: HTML TODO comments carry a ticket and, when asked, a date
rules.fix_reason: a ticket and a date are facts about the work that only the author knows; the engine can't invent them
rules.dont: <!-- TODO: swap in the final copy -->
rules.do: <!-- TODO(WEB-5): swap in the final copy -->
fix_steps: Open or find the ticket for the work and write it in the parentheses: `TODO(ABC-123): …`.
When the project asks for a date (`require_date`), or the work has a deadline, add it: `TODO(ABC-123, 2027-01-31): …`.
For an expired marker: do the work and delete the comment; or, if the work really moves, change the date and say why in the text.
If the comment is not a to-do, rewrite it so it does not open with the tag.

example.dont: Welcome
example.do: Welcome

rules.title: Repeated landmarks have distinct names
rules.fix_reason: the names need a human
fix_steps: Give each landmark of the same kind its own `aria-label`, or point `aria-labelledby` at its heading.

rules.title: Character references exist and are terminated
rules.fix_reason: the intended character is not always clear
fix_steps: Correct the name, or escape the `&` as `&` if no reference was meant.
End the reference with `;`.

rules.title: autocomplete values are valid
rules.fix_reason: the right field name depends on what the field collects
fix_steps: Pick the field name that describes the data (the WHATWG autofill list).
Order the tokens as described above, or use `off`.

example.dont:

fix_steps: Find a branch that decides one thing (a `switch` over a kind, a run of `if`s that validate input) and extract it into a well-named function that returns the result.

rules.title: No var or function at the top of a script

rules.title: Every feature flag read is registered, with an owner and a date it goes
rules.fix_reason: Keeping one branch of a flag removes the other branch's code; a person or agent accepts the diff.

presets.description: `[flags] presets`, for this rule only: the SDKs whose reads codelaw knows (launchdarkly, unleash, split, openfeature, growthbook, flagsmith)

accessors.description: `[flags] accessors`, for this rule only: calls with one `$NAME` slot that read a flag

inline.description: `[flags] inline`, for this rule only: `allow` or `registry-only`

warn_days.description: `[flags] warn_days`, for this rule only: how many days before `expires` a read warns

fix_steps: Unregistered: add the flag to `.codelaw/flags.toml` (`[[flag]] name, owner, ticket, expires`), or mark it inline above the read: `// codelaw-flag <name> expires YYYY-MM-DD owner @team`.

Expiring or expired: decide which branch stays. Set `keep = "on"` or `keep = "off"` on its registry entry and run `codelaw fix --unsafe`: an `if` or a conditional whose whole condition is the read keeps that branch. Where the read is anything else (`&&`, `!`, a variable), keep the branch by hand.
When the flag has no read left, `codelaw fix` removes its registry entry (`data/flag-registry`).
A flag meant to stay (a kill switch): `expires = "never"` with a `reason`.

rules.title: An inline flag marker agrees with the registry

presets.description: `[flags] presets`, for this rule only: the SDKs whose reads codelaw knows (launchdarkly, unleash, split, openfeature, growthbook, flagsmith)

accessors.description: `[flags] accessors`, for this rule only: calls with one `$NAME` slot that read a flag

inline.description: `[flags] inline`, for this rule only: `allow` or `registry-only`

warn_days.description: `[flags] warn_days`, for this rule only: how many days before `expires` a read warns

fix_steps: Run `codelaw fix`: a marker that disagrees with the registry is rewritten to match it, and a marker of a flag with no read left is removed.

A flag marked in several places with different values: add one `[[flag]]` entry for it to `.codelaw/flags.toml` with the values that are right, and delete the markers (or let `codelaw fix` rewrite them).
An unreadable marker: write it as `codelaw-flag <name> expires YYYY-MM-DD [owner …] [ticket …] [keep on|off] [reason …]`.

rules.fix_reason: which property the tag is for is the author's to say

rules.title: @property has a type
rules.fix_reason: the type is the author's to name; codelaw cannot infer it
fix_steps: Write the property's type in braces between `@property` and its name.

rules.title: A function that rejects documents @rejects
rules.fix_reason: when and why the promise rejects is the author's to describe
fix_steps: Add `@rejects {ErrorType} When ...` describing when the returned promise rejects.

rules.title: A function that returns a value documents @returns
rules.fix_reason: what the return value means is the author's to describe
fix_steps: Add `@returns {type} description` saying what the function gives back.

rules.title: @returns only where a value is returned
rules.fix_reason: whether to return the documented value or drop the tag is the author's call
fix_steps: Return the documented value, or remove the `@returns` tag (or make it `@returns {void}`).

rules.title: @returns says what is returned
rules.fix_reason: the description is the author's words
fix_steps: After the `@returns` type, write what the value is.

rules.title: @returns has a type
rules.fix_reason: the type is the author's to name; codelaw cannot infer it
fix_steps: Write the return type in braces right after `@returns`.

rules.title: Type parameters are documented with @template
rules.fix_reason: each type parameter needs its own @template line with the author's description
fix_steps: Add `@template T description` for each type parameter, in order.

rules.title: @template says what the type parameter is
rules.fix_reason: the description is the author's words
fix_steps: After the type parameter's name, write what it stands for.

rules.title: A function that throws documents @throws
rules.fix_reason: when and why the function throws is the author's to describe
rules.do: * @throws {RangeError} When the text is not a number.
fix_steps: Add `@throws {ErrorType} When ...` describing when the function throws.

rules.title: @throws says when
rules.fix_reason: the description is the author's words
rules.do: * @throws {RangeError} When the text is not a number.
fix_steps: After the `@throws` type, write the condition that throws it.

rules.title: @throws has a type
rules.fix_reason: the type is the author's to name; codelaw cannot infer it
rules.dont: * @throws When the text is not a number.
rules.do: * @throws {RangeError} When the text is not a number.
fix_steps: Write the error's type in braces right after `@throws`.

rules.title: A generator that yields documents @yields
rules.fix_reason: what the yielded values mean is the author's to describe
fix_steps: Add `@yields {type} description` saying what each yielded value is.

rules.title: @yields only where a value is yielded
rules.fix_reason: whether to yield the documented value or drop the tag is the author's call
fix_steps: Yield the documented values, or remove the `@yields` tag.

rules.title: @yields says what is yielded
rules.fix_reason: the description is the author's words
fix_steps: After the `@yields` type, write what each yielded value is.

rules.title: @yields has a type
rules.fix_reason: the type is the author's to name; codelaw cannot infer it
fix_steps: Write the yielded values' type in braces right after `@yields`.

rules.title: No @ts-ignore or @ts-nocheck in JavaScript
rules.fix_reason: the reason the error is expected has to come from the author
rules.do: // @ts-expect-error: the fixture checks the checker's message
fix_steps: Fix the type error if you can.
Otherwise replace the comment with `// @ts-expect-error: <why>`.

example.do:
// @ts-expect-error: the fixture checks the checker's message
const n = Math.max("1");

rules.title: No {} type in JSDoc
rules.fix_reason: whether `object`, `unknown` or a real shape is meant is the author's call
fix_steps: Replace `{}` with `object` for any non-primitive, `unknown` for any value, or the object's real shape.

rules.title: target="_blank" with rel="noopener"
rules.fix_reason: `noreferrer` also drops the Referer header, which an analytics setup may expect

rules.title: a ||= b rather than a = a || b
rules.fix_reason: the operator of the rewrite depends on which of three patterns matched
fix_steps: Write `a ||= b`, `a &&= b` or `a ??= b`.

rules.title: matchAll() needs a global regex
rules.fix_reason: the call throws today; adding the `g` flag makes it run

rules.title: One class per file
rules.fix_reason: the class moves to another file and its users import it
fix_steps: Rewrite the code as the message says.

rules.title: Blocks nest no deeper than a maximum
rules.fix_reason: flattening nested blocks changes the function's structure; which guard to invert or which block to extract is the author's call

max.description: the most blocks that may nest inside one another in a function

fix_steps: Turn a guard into an early `return`, `continue` or `throw`, so the rest of the function sits one level up.
Extract the body of the innermost block into a well-named function.
Replace a nested pair of `if`s with one condition joined by `&&`.

rules.title: A file stays under a maximum number of lines
rules.fix_reason: splitting a file changes its structure; which exports belong together is the author's call

max.description: the most lines a file may have

skip_comments.description: lines that hold only a comment do not count

skip_imports.description: the import block does not count

fix_steps: Find a cohesive group of exports (a component and its helpers, one feature's types) and move it to a new module next to the file.
Import it back where it is used, or re-export it from the old file so callers do not change.
If the file is long on purpose, raise `max` for it in an `[[overrides]]` entry, or freeze it with `codelaw baseline add --rule js/max-lines`.

rules.title: A function stays under a maximum number of lines
rules.fix_reason: extracting part of a function changes its structure; where to cut and what to call the piece is the author's call

max.description: the most lines one function may span

skip_comments.description: lines that hold only a comment do not count

include_nested.description: the lines of an inner function count toward the outer one too

include_iife.description: measure an immediately invoked function, `(() => { … })()`, as a function of its own

ignore_names.description: a regular expression; functions named like this are exempt, e.g. "^(test|it|describe)"

fix_steps: Find a block inside the function that does one thing (a loop body, a branch, a run of statements that build one value).
Extract it into a well-named function, and pass in what it reads.
Repeat until each piece fits `max`. If the function is long on purpose, name it in `ignore_names`, or freeze it with `codelaw baseline add --rule js/max-lines-per-function`.

rules.title: A function takes at most a maximum number of parameters
rules.fix_reason: grouping parameters changes the function's signature and every call to it; which belong together is the author's call

max.description: the most parameters a function may take

ignore_names.description: a regular expression; parameters named like this do not count

ignore_overrides.description: skip a TypeScript `override` method: its signature is not yours

ignore_declarations.description: skip an overload signature, a `declare` function, an abstract method and a `.d.ts` file

ignore_constructor_injection.description: TypeScript: skip a constructor whose parameters are all parameter properties (Angular, NestJS)

rules.do: function createOrder({ customer, items, coupon, address }) {
fix_steps: Group the parameters that belong together into one options object: `createOrder({ customer, items, coupon, address })`.
Update the callers to pass the object, and give the destructured parameter a type in TypeScript.
If the signature is not yours to change, exempt it: an `override`, an overload and a `declare` function already are.

rules.title: Constructors are capitalised
rules.fix_reason: renaming the constructor changes its declaration and every use
fix_steps: Rewrite the code as the message says.

rules.title: new for constructors, no new for Symbol and BigInt
rules.fix_reason: `Date()` returns a string and `new Date()` an object, so adding `new` can change the value

rules.title: Name the rules a disable comment turns off
rules.fix_reason: which rules were meant is known only to the author
fix_steps: List the rule ids after the directive, separated by commas.

rules.title: A getter or setter does not use itself
rules.fix_reason: the backing field name (`#name`, `_name`) is the author's choice
fix_steps: Store the value in a private field (`#name`) and read or write that from the accessor.

rules.title: No & or | in a condition
rules.fix_reason: `&&` short-circuits and yields an operand rather than a number
fix_steps: Use `&&` for `&` and `||` for `|`; if a bit test was meant, compare it: `(flags & MASK) !== 0`.

rules.title: No spread of the accumulator in reduce
rules.fix_reason: pushing onto the accumulator changes the callback's shape; the author rewrites it
fix_steps: Mutate the accumulator (`acc.push(x); return acc;` or `acc[k] = v; return acc;`), or build the result with a loop.

rules.title: No alert, confirm or prompt
rules.fix_reason: the replacement is the app's own dialog or a log line, chosen by the author
fix_steps: Replace the call with the app's dialog component, or remove it.

rules.title: Not every branch the same
rules.fix_reason: which branch is wrong is the author's call
fix_steps: Change the branch that was meant to differ, or drop the condition.

rules.title: No Angular sanitiser bypass
rules.fix_reason: only the author knows whether the value is trusted
fix_steps: Sanitise the value with `DomSanitizer.sanitize`, or prove it is a constant the user cannot influence.

rules.title: Name the default export
rules.fix_reason: the name comes from the file name, which the rule does not read
fix_steps: Name the function or class after the file (`user-card.js` → `UserCard`).

rules.title: Wrap function references passed to array methods
rules.fix_reason: the wrapped function no longer receives the index and the array, which it may have used

rules.title: No concat() in a loop
rules.fix_reason: `push` mutates the array in place, which other holders of the old array would see
fix_steps: Use `a.push(...items)`, or build a list of parts in the loop and `.flat()` it once after.

rules.title: No fill() with an object
rules.fix_reason: the array length is not always in the same expression
fix_steps: Use `Array.from({ length: n }, () => value)`, which creates a new value for each slot.

rules.title: Array.from with a mapper rather than fill()
rules.fix_reason: `Array.from` may already have a mapper argument, and the fill value moves into a new arrow function
fix_steps: Move the fill value into a mapper: `Array.from({ length: n }, () => value)`.

rules.title: No unshift() or shift()
rules.fix_reason: switching ends changes the order the rest of the code reads
fix_steps: Push at the end and read from the end, or build a new array `[item, ...queue]` where a copy is wanted.

rules.title: arguments has no array methods
rules.fix_reason: the call throws today; `Array.from(arguments)` makes it run, on a copy, so a mutating method no longer touches `arguments`

rules.title: No thisArg to array callbacks
rules.fix_reason: a regular function callback that reads `this` would lose it

rules.title: No reduce()
rules.fix_reason: the loop needs a variable for the accumulator
fix_steps: Declare the accumulator with `let`, loop over the array with `for … of`, and update it in the body.

rules.title: toReversed() rather than reverse()
rules.fix_reason: `toReversed()` leaves the original untouched, which code later reading it may rely on either way

rules.title: toSorted() rather than sort()
rules.fix_reason: `toSorted()` leaves the original untouched, which code later reading it may rely on either way

rules.title: Math.min/max rather than sorting for one value
rules.fix_reason: which of `Math.min` and `Math.max` the comparator means is read from the comparator, which a template cannot do
rules.dont: const first = values.toSorted((a, b) => a - b)[0];
fix_steps: If the comparator sorts ascending, use `Math.min(...values)`; descending, `Math.max(...values)`. For objects, find the extreme with a `reduce` or a loop.

example.dont: const first = values.toSorted((a, b) => a - b)[0];

rules.title: toSpliced() rather than splice() for a copy
rules.fix_reason: `.toSpliced()` returns the new array rather than the removed items, so the surrounding code must change
fix_steps: If the removed items are what is wanted, use `.slice()`; if the changed array is, assign `.toSpliced(...)` to it.

rules.title: A Promise executor is not an async function
rules.fix_reason: the rewrite depends on what the executor does
fix_steps: If the executor only awaits and resolves, use the awaited promise directly.
Otherwise make the executor a plain function and handle errors with `reject`.

rules.title: No async callback in finally
rules.fix_reason: whether the cleanup must finish first decides the rewrite
fix_steps: Make the callback synchronous, or move the awaited cleanup into a `try … finally` in an async function.

rules.title: No member access on an await expression
rules.fix_reason: the destructuring depends on how the value is used next
fix_steps: Destructure the awaited value (`const { name } = await getUser()`) or assign it to a variable first.

rules.title: No await inside a loop
rules.fix_reason: the iterations may depend on each other; only the author knows if they can run together
fix_steps: Collect the promises and `await Promise.all(...)` after the loop, if the iterations are independent.

rules.title: No await inside Promise.all([...])
rules.fix_reason: the awaited promise no longer finishes before the others start
rules.dont: const [a, b] = await Promise.all([await loadA(), loadB()]);

example.dont: const [a, b] = await Promise.all([await loadA(), loadB()]);

rules.title: No barrel file
rules.fix_reason: every importer of the barrel must import from the real module
fix_steps: Rewrite the code as the message says.

rules.title: No bitwise operators
rules.fix_reason: whether `&&` / `||` was meant, or the bit operation is intended, is the author's call
fix_steps: Use `&&` or `||` if a logical operator was meant; otherwise turn the rule off for this line with a reason.

rules.title: A sort comparator returns a number
rules.fix_reason: the right comparator depends on the values compared (numbers, strings)
fix_steps: Return `a - b` for numbers, `a.localeCompare(b)` for strings.

rules.title: No arguments.callee or arguments.caller
rules.fix_reason: naming the function to refer to it changes its declaration
rules.do: const f = function self() { return self; };
fix_steps: Give the function a name and refer to it by that name.

example.do: const f = function self() { return self; };

rules.title: No let, const, function or class directly in a case
rules.fix_reason: another case may rely on the shared declaration
fix_steps: Wrap the case's statements in `{ … }`.
If another case uses the declaration, move it above the `switch`.

rules.title: No label inside a case
rules.fix_reason: whether a case or a label was meant is the author's call
fix_steps: Remove the label, or turn it into the `case` that was meant.

rules.title: No a < b < c
rules.fix_reason: the middle operand is evaluated twice in the rewrite
fix_steps: Split it into two comparisons joined by `&&`: `a < b && b < c`.

rules.title: charAt() compared with a longer string
rules.fix_reason: whether the code meant `startsWith`, a `slice` or a one-character string is the author's; the code is wrong in each case differently
fix_steps: To test a prefix at a position, use `$S.startsWith(str, i)`.
To compare one character, compare with that one character.

rules.title: A class name is not reassigned
rules.fix_reason: what the assignment was for is the author's call
fix_steps: Assign to a new variable instead of the class name.

rules.title: No http:// or ftp:// URLs
rules.fix_reason: whether the host supports TLS must be checked
fix_steps: Rewrite the code as the message says.

rules.title: No comparisons against -0
rules.fix_reason: whether `0` or `-0` was meant needs the author
fix_steps: To test for negative zero, use `Object.is(x, -0)`.
To test for zero of either sign, compare with `0`.

rules.title: No assignment in a condition, unless doubly parenthesised
rules.fix_reason: whether a comparison or an assignment was meant needs the author
fix_steps: If a comparison was meant, use `===`.
If the assignment is meant, wrap it in a second pair of parentheses.

rules.title: No console calls left in the code
rules.fix_reason: deleting the call also drops its arguments, which may have side effects; and a call whose value is used needs the author

allow.description: console methods that may stay, e.g. ["warn", "error"]

fix_steps: Delete the call (`codelaw fix --unsafe` does when the call is a whole statement).
If the output is wanted, report through the project's logger instead.
If the method should stay everywhere, add it to the rule's `allow` option.

rules.title: No leading or trailing space in console arguments
rules.fix_reason: trimming the string is a computed edit a template cannot make
fix_steps: Remove the leading or trailing space from the string.

rules.title: A const is not reassigned
rules.fix_reason: whether the variable should be `let` or the assignment should go is the author's call
fix_steps: If the value is meant to change, declare it with `let`.
Otherwise assign to a new variable.

rules.title: No binary expression whose result is fixed
rules.fix_reason: the intended grouping or comparison needs the author
fix_steps: Add the parentheses the expression was meant to have.
Or compare with the value that was meant.

rules.title: No conditions that are always true or always false
rules.fix_reason: whether to remove the branch or fix the condition needs the author
fix_steps: If the branch is dead, remove it.
Otherwise replace the constant with the condition that was meant.

rules.title: No clamp with its bounds swapped
rules.fix_reason: swapping the bounds makes the clamp work, which changes the value it returns
fix_steps: Swap the two bounds.

rules.title: No multiply by zero
rules.fix_reason: whether 0 or another factor was meant is the author's call
fix_steps: Write the constant, or the factor that was meant.

rules.title: A constructor returns no value
rules.fix_reason: the returned value may belong in a factory function
fix_steps: Remove the value, or move the logic into a static factory method.

rules.title: No continue
rules.fix_reason: inverting the condition restructures the loop body
fix_steps: Invert the condition and wrap the rest of the body in an `if`.

rules.title: No control characters in regular expressions
rules.fix_reason: which character was meant needs the author
fix_steps: Use the named escape (`\t`, `\n`, `\f`) if one was meant.
Otherwise remove the control character from the pattern.

rules.title: No default exports
rules.fix_reason: every importer of the default export must change
fix_steps: Give the exported value a name and export it with `export { name }`.
Change every `import x from` of this module to `import { name } from`.

rules.title: Import by name, not the default
rules.fix_reason: the module's named export for this value is not written in this file
fix_steps: Find the named export the module offers for this value (export it by name if it has none).
Import it by that name: `import { name } from "module"`.

rules.title: No delete on a variable
rules.fix_reason: what the code meant to clear is a decision
fix_steps: To clear the value, assign `undefined` or a fresh value.
To remove a property, `delete obj.key`.

rules.title: No regex starting with =
rules.fix_reason: the edit inside the pattern is not a template edit
fix_steps: Write the leading `=` as `[=]`.

rules.title: No document.cookie
rules.fix_reason: the replacement is async and its arguments come from parsing the string
fix_steps: Use `cookieStore.set(name, value)` or a cookie library that encodes the value and attributes.

rules.title: No direct writes to document.cookie
rules.fix_reason: moving to the Cookie Store API makes the code asynchronous
fix_steps: Use `cookieStore.set(name, value)` or the project's cookie helper.

rules.title: x > a || x === a is x >= a
rules.fix_reason: the operator of the rewrite depends on which of four patterns matched
fix_steps: Write `x >= y` or `x <= y`.

rules.title: No two parameters share a name
rules.fix_reason: which parameter was meant can't be known from the code
fix_steps: Rename the duplicate parameter.
Update the body to read the parameter it meant.

rules.title: No two class members share a name
rules.fix_reason: which of the two members to keep is a decision
fix_steps: Decide which declaration is right.
Remove or rename the other.

rules.title: No two conditions in an if/else-if chain are the same
rules.fix_reason: what the second condition should have been is a decision
fix_steps: Find the repeated condition.
Correct it to the case it was meant to handle, or remove the dead branch.

rules.title: No two keys in an object literal are the same
rules.fix_reason: which value should win can't be known from the code
fix_steps: Decide which value the key should have.
Remove the other entry, or give it its own key.

rules.title: No two case labels in a switch are the same
rules.fix_reason: which label was meant is a decision
fix_steps: Find the label that was meant to test something else.
Correct it, or merge the two bodies.

rules.title: One import per module
rules.fix_reason: merging the specifier lists is a computed edit
fix_steps: Rewrite the code as the message says.

example.dont:
import { a } from "./util";
import { b } from "./util";

rules.title: No repeated literal in new Set([...])
rules.fix_reason: whether the repeat is a typo for another value is the author's call
fix_steps: Remove the repeated value, or replace it with the one that was meant.

rules.title: No computed access on a namespace import
rules.fix_reason: naming the exports used means the author choosing them
fix_steps: Import the names you need and pick between them explicitly (a `switch` or an object of the imports).

example.dont:
import * as icons from './icons';
export const icon = (name) => icons[name];

rules.title: No else after return
rules.fix_reason: unwrapping the block re-indents its statements, and a declaration in it could clash with one outside
fix_steps: Delete `else {` and its closing `}`, and move its statements up one level.

rules.title: No empty blocks
rules.fix_reason: whether to fill the block, remove it or document it needs the author
fix_steps: If the block is unfinished, write its code.
If it's meant to be empty, put a comment in it saying why.

rules.title: No empty character classes in regular expressions
rules.fix_reason: which characters the class should hold needs the author
fix_steps: Put the characters the class should match inside it.
If `[]` was meant literally, escape it: `\[\]`.

rules.title: No empty file
rules.fix_reason: whether to delete the file or fill it is the author's call
fix_steps: Delete the file, or write the code it was meant to hold.

rules.title: No empty functions
rules.fix_reason: the function's code, or the comment explaining why it is empty, is the author's
fix_steps: Write the function's code, or a comment saying why it does nothing.

rules.title: No empty destructuring patterns
rules.fix_reason: what the pattern was meant to bind needs the author
fix_steps: Name the properties to bind inside the pattern, or remove it.

rules.title: A test has a title
rules.fix_reason: the title is human-written
fix_steps: Rewrite the code as the message says.

rules.title: No == null
rules.fix_reason: whether `undefined` should match too decides between `=== null` and an explicit two-way check
fix_steps: Write `=== null` (or `x === null || x === undefined` if both were meant).

rules.title: No == or != as a for loop end test
rules.fix_reason: which relational operator is right depends on the direction
fix_steps: Use `<`, `<=`, `>` or `>=` in the direction the counter moves.

rules.title: Multiplying by zero erases the value
rules.fix_reason: `0` is the result for finite numbers only: `NaN * 0` is `NaN`, a BigInt needs `0n`, and the other operand's side effects go

rules.title: No eval
rules.fix_reason: what replaces it depends on what the string held
fix_steps: Parse data with `JSON.parse`, or call the function the string named directly.

rules.title: A caught error is not reassigned
rules.fix_reason: where the original error should go is a decision
fix_steps: Use a new variable for the new value.
Keep the original error, e.g. as `{ cause: err }`.

rules.title: No changes to built-in prototypes
rules.fix_reason: the method becomes a standalone function, which changes every call site
fix_steps: Write a standalone function that takes the value as its argument.

rules.title: No bind() on a function that does not use this
No needless !! or Boolean() in a condition
No label that is not needed
rules.fix_reason: removing the label token from the statement is not a template edit
fix_steps: Delete the label after `break` or `continue`; delete the label itself if nothing else uses it.

rules.title: A switch case does not fall through into the next by accident
rules.fix_reason: whether the fall-through is intended needs the author
fix_steps: If the case should stop, end it with `break` (or `return`).
If it should fall through, say so with a `// falls through` comment before the next case.

rules.title: flat, not flatMap of the identity
rules.fix_reason: `flat()` and `flatMap` agree on arrays; review on an object whose `flat` differs

rules.title: No focused tests left in the suite
rules.fix_reason: dropping the focus puts every other test in the file back in the run, and tests that were hidden behind it may fail; the author should see that
fix_steps: Remove the focus: `it.only(…)` becomes `it(…)`, `fit` becomes `it`, `fdescribe` becomes `describe` (`codelaw fix --unsafe` does).
Run the whole suite once; tests that were hidden may now fail, and that is the point.

rules.title: for…of rather than forEach
rules.fix_reason: a `return` in the callback becomes `continue`, and an index parameter becomes `.entries()`
fix_steps: Rewrite as `for (const item of items) { … }`; turn `return` into `continue`; for an index parameter use `for (const [i, item] of items.entries())`.

rules.title: A function declaration is not reassigned
rules.fix_reason: what the assignment was for is the author's call
fix_steps: Assign to a new variable instead.
If the function must be replaceable, declare it with `let` as a function expression.

rules.title: No assignment to built-in globals
rules.fix_reason: the intended variable needs a name of its own
fix_steps: Declare a local variable with its own name.

rules.title: Number.isFinite, not the global isFinite
rules.fix_reason: `Number.isFinite` does not convert its argument, so a numeric string now gives `false`; review the call

rules.title: Number.isNaN, not the global isNaN
rules.fix_reason: `Number.isNaN` does not convert its argument, so `'abc'` now gives `false`; review the call

rules.title: No properties on the global object
rules.fix_reason: readers of the global become importers of a module
fix_steps: Rewrite the code as the message says.

rules.title: No this at the top level
rules.fix_reason: whether `globalThis` or `undefined` was meant is the author's call
fix_steps: Rewrite the code as the message says.

rules.title: No hard-coded IP address
rules.fix_reason: the configuration key is the author's choice
fix_steps: Rewrite the code as the message says.

rules.title: No password in the code
rules.fix_reason: the secret's new home is the author's choice
fix_steps: Rewrite the code as the message says.

rules.title: No secret in a variable name
rules.fix_reason: the secret's new home is the owner's choice
fix_steps: Move the value to a secret store or the environment, read it at runtime, and rotate the committed one.

rules.title: No repeated condition in an if chain
rules.fix_reason: which condition was meant is the author's call
fix_steps: Correct the repeated condition, or remove the dead branch.

rules.title: No identical operands
rules.fix_reason: which operand was meant is the author's call
fix_steps: Correct the operand that was meant to be different, or replace the expression with its constant result.

rules.title: No empty catch
rules.fix_reason: what to do with the error is the author's call
fix_steps: Rewrite the code as the message says.

rules.title: Explicit conversions, not !!x or +x
rules.fix_reason: the call to write depends on the operator matched
fix_steps: Write `Boolean(x)` for `!!x` and `Number(x)` for `+x`.

rules.title: No string code in setTimeout
rules.fix_reason: turning the string into a function means writing that code
fix_steps: Pass a function: `setTimeout(() => refresh(), 1000)`.

rules.title: An imported binding is not reassigned
rules.fix_reason: the new value needs a variable of its own
