rules.title: Number.isNaN rather than isNaN
rules.fix_reason: the `Number` method does not convert its argument, so a string gives a different answer

rules.title: 0b101 rather than parseInt("101", 2)
rules.fix_reason: the literal's prefix depends on the radix, which a template cannot choose
fix_steps: Write `0b…` for radix 2, `0o…` for 8 and `0x…` for 16, with the same digits.

rules.title: { ...a } rather than Object.assign({}, a)
rules.fix_reason: `Object.assign` runs setters on the target and a spread defines properties, which differs for a getter-only source

rules.title: #private rather than _private
rules.fix_reason: every use of the member must change, and outside code that reads it breaks
fix_steps: Rewrite the code as the message says.

rules.title: Reject with an Error
rules.fix_reason: the error class and message are the author's
fix_steps: Pass `new Error(message)`.

rules.title: Promise.resolve rather than new Promise(r => r(x))
rules.fix_reason: `Promise.resolve` returns a promise given as `$X` unchanged, where the constructor wraps it

rules.title: querySelector rather than getElementById
rules.fix_reason: the selector string is built from the id, which a template cannot escape
fix_steps: Write `document.querySelector("#id")` (escape the id with `CSS.escape` if it is not a plain name).

rules.title: queueMicrotask rather than Promise.resolve().then
rules.fix_reason: an error thrown by the callback is reported instead of rejecting a promise nobody reads

rules.title: A regex literal rather than new RegExp("…")
rules.fix_reason: the literal is created once per evaluation of the enclosing code, a `RegExp` call once per call; with the `g` flag `lastIndex` then differs

rules.title: regex.test() rather than match() in a condition
Response.json rather than new Response(JSON.stringify())
rules.fix_reason: the response gains a `Content-Type: application/json` header

rules.title: Rest parameters instead of arguments
rules.fix_reason: the parameter list has to be rewritten by hand
fix_steps: Add a rest parameter `...args` to the function.
Replace each use of `arguments` with it.

rules.title: Return the condition, not true/false
rules.fix_reason: a non-boolean condition needs `Boolean(…)` or `!`, decided per pattern
fix_steps: Rewrite the code as the message says.

rules.title: One push() with several items
rules.fix_reason: merging two statements is a cross-statement edit
fix_steps: Rewrite the code as the message says.

example.dont:
const max = Math.max.apply(null, values);
const min = least.apply(null, values);
example.do:
const max = Math.max.apply(null, values);
const min = least(...values);

rules.title: [...x] rather than Array.from(x)
rules.fix_reason: `Array.from` accepts array-likes (an object with `length`) that spread rejects

rules.title: replaceAll() rather than replace with a /g regex
startsWith() rather than a ^ regex test
rules.fix_reason: the string literal is the pattern without its anchor, which a template cannot strip
fix_steps: Write `s.startsWith("…")` with the text after `^`.

rules.title: structuredClone rather than JSON round-trip
rules.fix_reason: dates stay `Date` objects, `undefined` keys are kept, and a function throws instead of being dropped

rules.title: Template literal rather than string concatenation
rules.fix_reason: escaping the parts into one template literal is a computed edit
fix_steps: Write one template literal: each string part as text, each other operand as `${…}`.

rules.title: .catch() rather than a second then() argument
rules.fix_reason: `.catch()` also catches errors from `show`, which changes behaviour
fix_steps: Rewrite the code as the message says.

rules.title: Top-level await rather than an async IIFE
rules.fix_reason: the file must be a module, and a rejection now fails the import
fix_steps: Rewrite the code as the message says.

rules.title: while rather than for(;;) with only a condition
A rethrown error keeps the caught one as its cause
rules.fix_reason: the new error class must accept an options argument
rules.do: throw new Error("Load failed", { cause: err });

rules.title: A then callback returns or throws
rules.fix_reason: what the callback should return is the author's to decide
fix_steps: Return the value the next step needs — often the inner promise the callback started — or throw if the callback found an error.

rules.title: No new Promise
rules.fix_reason: replacing an executor means choosing an `async` function or a promisified API
rules.dont: const wait = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
fix_steps: Write the function as `async`, or wrap the callback API with `util.promisify`.

example.dont: const wait = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

rules.title: A promise chain is returned, awaited or ends in catch
rules.fix_reason: where the error should go — a `.catch()`, a `return` or an `await` — is the author's decision
fix_steps: Add a `.catch()` at the end of the chain that handles or reports the error, or `return` / `await` the chain so the caller does.

rules.title: No node-style callback is called inside a then or catch
rules.fix_reason: moving the call out of the promise needs a choice between `nodeify`-style wrappers, `setImmediate` or rewriting the caller
fix_steps: Return the promise to the caller, or call the callback outside the chain (for example in `setImmediate`) so an error it throws is not swallowed.

rules.title: A promise executor settles once on each path
rules.fix_reason: whether the first or the second call is the right one is the author's call
fix_steps: Add the missing `return` after the first call, or delete the call that should not run.

rules.title: Promise is imported, not the global
rules.fix_reason: which promise library to import is the project's choice
fix_steps: Import the promise implementation the project uses (`import Promise from "bluebird"`) at the top of the file.

example.do:
import Promise from "bluebird";
const p = Promise.resolve(1);

rules.title: Promise chains are flattened, not nested
rules.fix_reason: flattening a chain moves code between callbacks and may need values carried along
fix_steps: Return the inner promise from the outer callback and move its `.then()` up to the outer chain.

rules.title: Promise's static methods are called without new
No promise chain inside a node-style callback
rules.fix_reason: converting the callback API to promises (for example with `util.promisify`) is a refactor of the caller
fix_steps: Wrap the callback API with `util.promisify` (or write a promise version) and chain or `await` it.

example.do:
const text = await readFile(path);
show(await parse(text));

rules.title: A finally callback returns nothing
rules.fix_reason: whether the value belongs in a `.then()` before the `finally` or should be dropped is the author's call
fix_steps: Move the value into a `.then()` before the `.finally()`, or delete the `return` value if it was not meant to change the result.

rules.title: A then or catch callback returns the value, not Promise.resolve or Promise.reject
rules.fix_reason: turning `return Promise.reject(e)` into `throw e` changes the statement's shape inside code the author may want to restructure
fix_steps: Replace `return Promise.resolve(x)` with `return x`.
Replace `return Promise.reject(e)` with `throw e`.

rules.title: A promise executor names its parameters resolve and reject
rules.fix_reason: renaming a parameter is safe only when every use in the executor is renamed with it; rename it by hand or with the editor
rules.dont: const p = new Promise((ok, fail) => setTimeout(ok, 10));
rules.do: const p = new Promise((resolve, reject) => setTimeout(resolve, 10));
fix_steps: Rename the first parameter to `resolve` and the second to `reject`, and every use of each in the executor.

example.dont: const p = new Promise((ok, fail) => setTimeout(ok, 10));
example.do: const p = new Promise((resolve, reject) => setTimeout(resolve, 10));

rules.title: async and await, not callbacks
rules.fix_reason: turning a callback API into a promise changes every caller
fix_steps: Make the function `async` (or return a promise), drop the callback parameter, and `await` it at each call site.

rules.title: await, not then
rules.fix_reason: moving a chain to `await` needs an `async` function and may restructure the error handling
fix_steps: Make the enclosing function `async` and replace `p.then((x) => …)` with `const x = await p;`.

rules.title: catch, not a second then argument
rules.fix_reason: `.catch(b).then(a)` passes the handler's result on to `a` where `.then(a, b)` did not; review the order before accepting

rules.title: Only standard Promise methods
rules.fix_reason: the standard replacement depends on what the library method did
fix_steps: Replace the library method with the standard ones (`Promise.all(items.map(f))` for `Promise.map`) or import the library explicitly.

rules.title: Promise methods get the number of arguments they take
rules.fix_reason: which argument is the intended one cannot be known from the call
fix_steps: Pass the arguments the method takes: one value to `resolve`/`reject`, one iterable to `all`/`race`, one or two handlers to `then`, one to `catch`/`finally`.

rules.title: Math.random() in security code
rules.fix_reason: whether the value needs to be unpredictable is the author's call
fix_steps: Rewrite the code as the message says.

rules.title: No files in /tmp
rules.fix_reason: the private directory's lifetime is the author's choice
fix_steps: Create a private directory with `fs.mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "prefix-"))` and write inside it.

rules.title: parseInt gets a radix
rules.fix_reason: base 10 is the usual intent, but a string with a `0x` prefix parses differently with it

rules.title: No quantifier whose minimum is misleading
rules.fix_reason: lowering the minimum to 0 says what the pattern does, but the author may have meant the element to be required
fix_steps: Write the minimum as 0 if empty is meant.
Otherwise make what is repeated require a character.

rules.title: Control characters are written with their control escape
String literals in a class hold one character each
rules.fix_reason: moving a string out of the class into an alternation changes the pattern's structure, which the author decides
fix_steps: Move the multi-character string out of the class: `(?:abc|[x])`.

rules.title: Characters up to U+00FF are written as hexadecimal escapes
A negated class of one escape is the negated escape
No element the assertion before it contradicts
rules.fix_reason: removing the element or its quantifier says what the pattern does, which may not be what was meant
fix_steps: Make the element required, or remove it.

rules.title: No character listed twice in a class
No alternative that repeats or is covered by an earlier one
rules.fix_reason: removing the alternative changes the pattern's text; check it wasn't a typo for a different one
fix_steps: Remove the alternative, or fix the one that was meant.

rules.title: No empty alternative
rules.fix_reason: making the group optional matches the same strings, but a capturing group then captures nothing instead of the empty string
fix_steps: Make the group optional with `?`, or remove the stray `|`.

rules.title: No capturing group that captures nothing
rules.fix_reason: what the group should capture is the author's to write
fix_steps: Put what should be captured inside the group, or remove it.

rules.title: No character class that matches no character
rules.fix_reason: which characters the class was meant to hold is the author's to write
fix_steps: List the characters that were meant.

rules.title: No empty group
rules.fix_reason: auto for a non-capturing group (removing it changes nothing); a capturing one is reported without an edit, since its number is used

rules.title: No lookaround that can match the empty string
rules.fix_reason: what the lookaround should check is the author's to write
fix_steps: Make the lookaround require the characters it should check.

rules.title: No empty string literal in a class
rules.fix_reason: which strings the literal should hold is the author's to write
fix_steps: Write the strings the literal should hold, or remove it.

rules.title: No lookaround nested at the edge of another of its kind
No lazy quantifier at the end of the pattern
rules.fix_reason: the lazy quantifier at the end always takes its minimum; the edit writes that, which may not be what was meant
fix_steps: Write the minimum it matches, or make it greedy if the range was meant.

rules.title: No legacy `RegExp` static properties
rules.fix_reason: reading the match result instead of the global properties moves code to where the match is made
fix_steps: Keep the match result (`const m = re.exec(s)`) and read `m[1]`.

rules.title: No capturing group whose start the quantifier before it always takes
rules.fix_reason: making the quantifier before the group lazy changes what it matches; it is offered for an agent or a person to accept
fix_steps: Make the quantifier before it lazy, or narrow what it matches.

rules.title: No quantifier on part of a character
`replaceAll` and `matchAll` get a regular expression with the `g` flag
rules.fix_reason: adding `g` makes a call that throws work; the result is what was meant, but the behaviour changes

rules.title: Only standard regular expression flags
rules.fix_reason: removing the flag keeps the pattern standard, but which flag was meant may be another
fix_steps: Replace the flag with the standard one that was meant, or remove it.

rules.title: No obscure character range
fix_steps: List the characters, or use escapes for both ends.

rules.title: No octal escape
rules.fix_reason: the escape may have been meant as a backreference; the hexadecimal form keeps what it matches
fix_steps: Write the character as a hexadecimal escape, or fix the backreference.

rules.title: No backreference to a group that may not take part
rules.fix_reason: whether the group should always take part is the author's decision
fix_steps: Make the group required, or move the backreference inside the same optional part.

rules.title: No backslash that stands for itself
No exponential backtracking
rules.fix_reason: auto when one alternative of a repeated alternation matches a subset of another (it is removed, the language is the same); a repeated sequence with an unbounded quantifier is reported without an edit
fix_steps: Remove the overlap between the alternatives, or make the parts of the repeated sequence exclusive.

rules.title: No unanchored pattern that starts with an unbounded quantifier
rules.fix_reason: an anchor or a different quantifier changes what the pattern finds; the author decides
fix_steps: Anchor the pattern, or rewrite it so the quantifier can't restart at every position.

rules.title: No lookaround around a single assertion
No quantifier nested trivially in another
No capturing group whose capture is never read
No assertion that always succeeds or always fails
rules.fix_reason: removing an assertion that always succeeds keeps what the pattern matches, but one that always fails needs the author
fix_steps: Remove an assertion that always succeeds; rethink the pattern where one always fails.

rules.title: No replacement reference to a group that doesn't exist
fix_steps: Escape the dollar sign as `$$` (what the code does now), or reference an existing group.

rules.title: No useless escape in a regular expression
No lazy quantifier that can't be lazy
No non-capturing group that groups nothing
No range of one or two characters
No set operand that changes nothing
No string literal of single characters
No quantifier that repeats zero times
rules.fix_reason: removing the element keeps what the pattern matches, but it was probably meant to be there
fix_steps: Remove the element, or give the quantifier the count that was meant.

rules.title: No ranged quantifier at the edge of a lookaround
rules.fix_reason: the quantifier's minimum gives the same result; the edit is offered since the range may have been meant elsewhere
fix_steps: Write the minimum.

rules.title: No adjacent quantifiers that one quantifier covers
Single-character alternatives are a character class
A dollar sign in a replacement is written `$$`
A captured text put back unchanged is matched with a lookaround
rules.fix_reason: matching with a lookaround changes which text a global replacement consumes, so overlapping matches can differ
fix_steps: Turn the group into a lookbehind (or lookahead) and drop the `$1`.

rules.title: A named group is referred to by name
Capturing groups are named
rules.fix_reason: the group's name is the author's to choose
fix_steps: Give the group a name, and read it as `match.groups.name`.

rules.title: A named group is put in a replacement by name
A lookaround that is a predefined assertion is written as one
A repeated element is written with a quantifier
Consecutive letters or digits are a range
`RegExp#exec` over `String#match` without `g`
rules.fix_reason: `String#match` on a receiver that isn't a string may behave differently; the edit is for an agent or a person to accept
fix_steps: Call `exec` on the regular expression with the string.

rules.title: `RegExp#test` when only whether it matches is used
rules.fix_reason: `String#match` on a receiver that isn't a string may behave differently; the edit is for an agent or a person to accept
fix_steps: Call `test`.

rules.title: A named group is read from `groups`
A negative lookahead before a class is a set subtraction
An astral character is one code point escape
Regular expressions use the `u` flag
rules.fix_reason: auto when adding `u` can't change what the pattern matches (ASCII only, no `.`, no negation, no `i`); otherwise reported without an edit

rules.title: Regular expressions use the `v` flag
rules.fix_reason: auto when switching to `v` can't change what the pattern matches; otherwise reported without an edit

rules.title: Set operations in their simplest form
Alternatives whose order doesn't matter are sorted
Regular expressions use strict syntax
rules.fix_reason: auto for every form but a quantified lookahead, which is reported without an edit

rules.title: Unicode escapes use the code point form
Unicode properties in their usual form
Both cases of every letter means the `i` flag
No ./ in a relative URL
rules.fix_reason: stripping the prefix is a computed edit
fix_steps: Rewrite the code as the message says.

rules.title: replaceAll() needs a global regex
rules.fix_reason: the call throws today; adding the `g` flag makes it run

rules.title: An async function awaits something
rules.fix_reason: whether `async` or an `await` is missing is the author's call
fix_steps: If the function does wait on something, add the `await`; otherwise remove `async` and check its callers do not rely on a promise.

rules.title: Escape values in a selector
rules.fix_reason: which parts are values is the author's call
fix_steps: Rewrite the code as the message says.

rules.title: JSON imports say with { type: "json" }
rules.fix_reason: a bundler that does not support import attributes may then reject the file

rules.title: Touch and wheel listeners are passive
rules.fix_reason: a passive listener can no longer call `preventDefault()`

rules.title: postMessage names its target origin
rules.fix_reason: the origin to trust is the author's choice
fix_steps: Pass the exact origin the message is for, such as `location.origin` or the iframe's origin.

rules.title: Regular expressions use the u or v flag
rules.fix_reason: the flag makes the pattern stricter, so an escape that was ignored becomes a syntax error
fix_steps: Add `u` after the closing slash and check that the pattern still compiles.

rules.title: A generator function yields
rules.fix_reason: whether to yield or to drop the `*` needs the author
fix_steps: Add the `yield` the generator was meant to have, or remove the `*`.

rules.title: A skipped test has a reason and an expiry
rules.fix_reason: why a test is off, and until when, is a fact only the author knows; the engine can't write it
rules.do: // SKIP(SHOP-77, 2027-01-31): flaky on the CI clock
fix_steps: Write the reason, the ticket that tracks the fix and the date you will look again, on the line above: `// SKIP(ABC-123, 2027-01-31): reason`.
For an expired skip: fix the test and remove the skip; or, if it really must stay off, move the date and say why in the reason.
If the test is not needed, delete it.

rules.title: Keep the HSTS header
rules.fix_reason: HSTS commits the domain to HTTPS for its lifetime; the change closes access that something may rely on

rules.title: No break at the end of the last case
A Symbol has a description
rules.fix_reason: the description is the author's
fix_steps: Pass a short description: `Symbol('cache key')`.

rules.title: Write the encoding as "utf8"
rules.fix_reason: an API outside Node (such as `TextDecoder` in old engines) may expect the hyphenated name

rules.title: JavaScript and TypeScript TODO comments carry a ticket and, when asked, a date
rules.fix_reason: a ticket and a date are facts about the work that only the author knows; the engine can't invent them
fix_steps: Open or find the ticket for the work and write it in the parentheses: `TODO(ABC-123): …`.
When the project asks for a date (`require_date`), or the work has a deadline, add it: `TODO(ABC-123, 2027-01-31): …`.
For an expired marker: do the work and delete the comment; or, if the work really moves, change the date and say why in the text.
If the comment is not a to-do, rewrite it so it does not open with the tag.

rules.title: Verify TLS certificates
rules.fix_reason: the right fix is a trusted CA, which is configuration outside the code; the change closes access that something may rely on

rules.title: Verify the TLS host name
rules.fix_reason: the right check is the default one, or a pinned identity the author chooses
fix_steps: Rewrite the code as the message says.

rules.title: No assignment to a for loop counter in its body
rules.fix_reason: the rewrite (a `while` loop, a `continue`) depends on intent
fix_steps: Move the change into the loop's update, use `continue`, or rewrite it as a `while` loop.

rules.title: Use the project's function instead of the one it wraps

replacements.description: a dotted path to { use, from, drop_in?, allow_in? }: `use` is the function or variable to call instead, `from` the module it comes from, `drop_in` lets `codelaw fix` swap it in and add the import, `allow_in` lists globs of files exempt (the wrapper itself)

fix_steps: With `drop_in = true`, run `codelaw fix`: the path becomes `use` and the import is added when the file lacks it.
Without `drop_in`, change the call by hand: the replacement takes other arguments or returns another shape.
In the wrapper's own file, add the file to `allow_in` rather than the call to the baseline.

rules.title: Test for NaN with Number.isNaN
rules.fix_reason: the comparison's operator decides whether to negate
fix_steps: Replace `x === NaN` or `x == NaN` with `Number.isNaN(x)`.
Replace `x !== NaN` or `x != NaN` with `!Number.isNaN(x)`.

rules.title: Plain decimal numbers as object keys
rules.fix_reason: the decimal form has to be computed from the literal, which codelaw's fix templates cannot do
fix_steps: Write the key's decimal value (`0x10` → `16`, `1e2` → `100`).

rules.title: typeof is compared with a type it can return
rules.fix_reason: which type was meant needs the author
fix_steps: Correct the string to the type that was meant.

rules.title: No TLS 1.0 or 1.1
rules.fix_reason: very old clients will no longer connect
fix_steps: Set the property to its secure value, or remove it to take the secure default, and confirm nothing relies on the open setting.

rules.title: No external entities in XML parsing
rules.fix_reason: a document that needs entities must be trusted first
fix_steps: Remove `noent: true`; parse only trusted documents if entities are required.

rules.title: Variable first in a comparison
rules.fix_reason: swapping the operands changes their evaluation order, which matters if either has a side effect

rules.title: No key twice in one JSON object
rules.fix_reason: which of the two values was meant can't be known from the file
fix_steps: Decide which value the key should have.
Delete the other entry, or move it under a key of its own.

rules.title: package.json dependency lists are sorted by name
package.json declares engines.node
rules.fix_reason: the supported Node.js range is a project decision; the fix inserts the `node` option, which may not be the right range

node.description: the range the fix writes into `engines.node`

rules.title: package.json matches its schema
rules.fix_reason: a value the schema rejects is wrong in a way only its author knows how to correct
fix_steps: Read the message: it names the field and the form the schema expects.
Rewrite the value in that form, or remove the field if it was a mistake.
Run `codelaw check` on the file again until it is clean.

rules.title: package.json scripts are sorted by name
tsconfig.json matches its schema
rules.fix_reason: a misspelt or misshapen option has several possible meanings; the author picks the one they intended
fix_steps: Read the message: it names the option and what the schema expects, and suggests the option meant when the name is misspelt.
Correct the name or the value; remove an option TypeScript no longer has.
Run `codelaw check` on the file again until it is clean.

rules.title: tsconfig.json turns on strict mode
rules.fix_reason: turning on strict mode can surface type errors the code then has to fix

rules.title: No $ before shell commands that show no output
Link text says where the link goes
rules.fix_reason: describing the target needs the author

prohibited_texts.description: link texts that say nothing about the target, compared ignoring case and punctuation

fix_steps: Say in a few words what the link leads to.
Make those words the link text.

rules.title: Fenced code blocks name their language
rules.fix_reason: which language the code is in can't always be told from the code
fix_steps: Work out what the block holds.
Add its language after the opening fence, or `text` when it is plain output.

rules.title: A document starts with its title heading
rules.fix_reason: the title text needs the author

level.description: the level of the title heading

allow_preamble.description: allow text before the title heading

fix_steps: Write a heading that names the document.
Put it first, above any introduction.

rules.title: Heading levels go down one at a time
rules.fix_reason: the fix raises the skipped heading and its subsections, which changes the outline readers and tools see

Run the installer.

No blank line inside a blockquote

rules.title: Headings are headings, not bold lines
rules.fix_reason: which heading level the line should become depends on the outline

rules.title: Links have a destination
rules.fix_reason: where the link should go needs the author

Write that destination, or remove the link and keep its text.

rules.title: No raw HTML in Markdown
rules.fix_reason: the Markdown equivalent, if there is one, needs the author

allowed_elements.description: element names that may be used, such as `details` or `kbd`

rules.title: No punctuation at the end of a heading

punctuation.description: the characters a heading may not end with

rules.title: Proper names are spelled as the project spells them

names.description: the names, as they are spelled

code_blocks.description: check fenced and indented code blocks too

rules.title: Reference links use a label that is defined
rules.fix_reason: where the reference should point needs the author

ignored_labels.description: labels never reported (`x` is a task-list checkbox)

shortcut_syntax.description: also check `[label]` shortcuts, which plain bracketed text looks like

fix_steps: Check the label for a typo against the definitions.
Fix the label, or add the missing `[label]: url` definition.

rules.title: Relative links point at a file that exists
rules.fix_reason: whether the file moved, was renamed or was never written needs the author
fix_steps: Find where the file went: `git log --follow --stat -- <path>` shows a rename.
Point the link at the file's new path, or remove the link if the file is gone.

example.dont:
<!-- docs/guide.md -->
Start with [the setup](./setup.md), then read the [FAQ](../FAQ.md).
<!-- docs/setup.md -->
# Setup
example.do:
<!-- docs/guide.md -->
Start with [the setup](./setup.md), then read the [FAQ](../FAQ.md).
<!-- docs/setup.md -->
# Setup
<!-- FAQ.md -->
# FAQ

rules.title: Documents follow the required outline
rules.fix_reason: the missing section is the author's to write

headings.description: the required headings, in order, with their `#` level; `*` and `+` match runs

fix_steps: Add or rename the headings to match the outline.

rules.title: One level-1 heading per document
rules.fix_reason: which heading is the title, and what level the others become, needs the author

level.description: the level of the title heading

fix_steps: Keep the heading that names the document at level 1.
Make the others level 2 and shift their subsections down to match.

rules.title: Table rows have as many cells as the header
rules.fix_reason: which cell is missing or extra needs the author
fix_steps: Compare the row with the header.
Add the missing cells or remove the extra ones, or add a header column if the data needs it.

example.do:
| Name | Type | Note |
| ---- | ---- | ---- |
| id | number | required |

rules.title: Markdown TODO comments carry a ticket and, when asked, a date
rules.fix_reason: a ticket and a date are facts about the work that only the author knows; the engine can't invent them
fix_steps: Open or find the ticket for the work and write it in the parentheses: `TODO(ABC-123): …`.
When the project asks for a date (`require_date`), or the work has a deadline, add it: `TODO(ABC-123, 2027-01-31): …`.
For an expired marker: do the work and delete the comment; or, if the work really moves, change the date and say why in the text.
If the comment is not a to-do, rewrite it so it does not open with the tag.

example.dont:
# Setup

<!-- TODO: document the proxy settings -->
example.do:
# Setup

<!-- TODO(DOC-22): document the proxy settings -->

rules.title: Google Fonts load with display=swap or optional
rules.fix_reason: `swap` and `optional` trade layout shift against fallback text differently; the author picks
fix_steps: Append `&display=swap` (or `&display=optional`) to the URL, or move the font to `next/font/google`.

rules.title: fonts.gstatic.com is preconnected
rules.fix_reason: the link's purpose is the author's to confirm
fix_steps: Add `rel="preconnect"` (and `crossOrigin=""`) to the link.

rules.title: An inline next/script has an id
rules.fix_reason: the id is the author's to name
fix_steps: Add a unique `id` to the `<Script>`.

example.do:
import Script from "next/script";
const s = <Script id="log">{`console.log(1)`}</Script>;

rules.title: Google Analytics through next/third-parties
rules.fix_reason: moving to the component changes how the tag is configured
fix_steps: Use `<GoogleAnalytics gaId="…" />` from `@next/third-parties/google`.

rules.title: No variable named module
rules.fix_reason: the variable needs a new name, chosen by the author
fix_steps: Rename the variable (`mod`, `entry`, …).

rules.title: Client components are not async
rules.fix_reason: the data loading moves to a server component or an effect, which restructures the code
fix_steps: Load the data in a server component and pass it as props, or use an effect or a data library in the client.

rules.title: beforeInteractive scripts live in the document
rules.fix_reason: moving the script to the document is a structural change
fix_steps: Move the `<Script>` into `pages/_document` or `app/layout`.

rules.title: No stylesheet link tags for local CSS
rules.fix_reason: importing the CSS moves it into the module graph
fix_steps: `import './styles.css'` in the page or layout, and remove the `<link>`.

rules.title: next/document only in _document
rules.fix_reason: the replacement — `next/head` or the layout — depends on what was imported
fix_steps: Use `next/head` in a page, or move the code into `pages/_document`.

rules.title: One Head in _document
rules.fix_reason: the two heads' contents have to be merged by hand
fix_steps: Merge the two `<Head>` elements into one.

rules.title: next/head, not head
rules.fix_reason: moving the tags into `next/head` changes the imports
fix_steps: `import Head from 'next/head'` and use `<Head>`.

rules.title: No next/head in _document
rules.fix_reason: the import is replaced by the document's own `Head`
fix_steps: Replace the import with `import { Head } from 'next/document'`.

rules.title: Link, not a, for internal pages
rules.fix_reason: switching to `<Link>` adds an import
fix_steps: `import Link from 'next/link'` and replace `<a>` with `<Link>`.

rules.title: next/image, not img
rules.fix_reason: `<Image>` needs a width and height or `fill`, which the author supplies
rules.do: const i = <Image src="/logo.png" alt="Logo" width={64} height={64} />;
fix_steps: `import Image from 'next/image'` and replace `` with ``, giving it `width` and `height` or `fill`.

example.do: const i = <Image src="/logo.png" alt="Logo" width={64} height={64} />;

rules.title: router.push, not location for in-app paths
rules.fix_reason: the router comes from a hook or import the author adds
fix_steps: Use `router.push(path)` from `next/navigation` (or `next/router`).

rules.title: Custom fonts in the document, not a page
rules.fix_reason: moving the font changes the app's font setup
fix_steps: Use `next/font/google`, or move the link to `pages/_document`.

rules.title: No next/script inside next/head
rules.fix_reason: the script moves to the page body
fix_steps: Move the `<Script>` into the page body.

rules.title: No styled-jsx in _document
rules.fix_reason: the styles move to a global stylesheet or `_app`
fix_steps: Move the styles to a global CSS file imported in `_app`.

rules.title: No synchronous scripts
rules.fix_reason: `async`, `defer` or `next/script` each change when the script runs
fix_steps: Add `async` or `defer`, or use `<Script>` from `next/script`.

rules.title: No title in _document's Head
rules.fix_reason: each page's title is the author's
fix_steps: Remove the `<title>` and set it in each page with `next/head`.

rules.title: Data-fetching functions are spelled right
rules.fix_reason: the intended name is almost always obvious, but renaming an export is confirmed by the author
fix_steps: Rename it to `getStaticProps`, `getStaticPaths` or `getServerSideProps`.

rules.title: No polyfill.io
rules.fix_reason: what to keep depends on which features the script was polyfilling
fix_steps: Remove the script; add a specific polyfill package only for a feature Next.js does not already cover.

rules.title: Return after calling the callback
rules.fix_reason: `return cb(...)` also makes the function return what the callback returns; callers of a callback-style function rarely read it

rules.title: module.exports, not the exports shortcut
rules.fix_reason: auto only where the file never reassigns `module.exports`, so both names are the same object

rules.title: require() at the top of the module
rules.fix_reason: a require inside a function may be deliberate lazy loading or a way round a require cycle; moving it changes when the module loads
fix_steps: Move the `require()` to the top of the file and bind it to a `const`.
If it is lazy on purpose (a heavy or optional module, a require cycle), keep it and add the file to the baseline.

rules.title: Handle the err argument
rules.fix_reason: what to do with the error (pass it on, log it, retry) is the author's decision
fix_steps: Check `err` first, and return early: pass it to your own callback, throw it, or log it.
If the error truly cannot happen, name the parameter `_err` to say so.

rules.title: Commands start with a Node.js hashbang, and nothing else has one
rules.fix_reason: removing the hashbang of a script someone runs directly (`./tool.js`) stops it running
fix_steps: On a command `bin` names, make the first line `#!/usr/bin/env node`.
On any other file, remove the hashbang, or add the file to `bin` if it is a command.

rules.title: No async Express route handlers
rules.fix_reason: forwarding the rejection needs the project's own wrapper or error middleware, whose name is not in this file
fix_steps: Wrap the handler: `app.get(path, (req, res, next) => handler(req, res).catch(next))`, or use the project's async wrapper.
On Express 5, which forwards rejections itself, exclude the files from this rule.

rules.title: Pass an Error, not a string, to the callback
rules.fix_reason: wrapping the message in `new Error(...)` changes the value the callback receives, from a string to an Error

rules.title: No deprecated Node.js APIs
rules.fix_reason: each deprecated API has its own replacement
fix_steps: Replace the call with the API the message names.

example.dont:
import { isArray } from "node:util";
export const ok = isArray([]);

rules.title: No assigning to exports
rules.fix_reason: whether `module.exports` or a property was meant needs the author
fix_steps: Assign to `module.exports`, or set properties on `exports` (`exports.name = …`).

rules.title: Imported packages must be declared
rules.fix_reason: which dependency field and version to add is the package owner's choice
fix_steps: Add the package to the nearest `package.json` (`dependencies` if the shipped code needs it, `devDependencies` if only tests and tooling do), with your package manager's `add` command.
A type-only import is satisfied by its `@types/` package.

rules.title: Required packages must be declared
rules.fix_reason: which dependency field and version to add is the package owner's choice
fix_steps: Add the package to the nearest `package.json` (`dependencies` if the shipped code needs it, `devDependencies` if only tests and tooling do), with your package manager's `add` command.

rules.title: Imported project paths must exist
rules.fix_reason: the right path depends on where the module went
fix_steps: Point the specifier at the file that exists (check the extension and the folder), or restore the missing file.
A path to a generated file the repo doesn't hold is reported too: generate it before `codelaw check`, or suppress the line with a reason.

rules.title: Required project paths must exist
rules.fix_reason: the right path depends on where the module went
fix_steps: Point the specifier at the file that exists (check the extension and the folder), or restore the missing file.

rules.title: Don't mix requires with other declarations
rules.fix_reason: splitting the declaration needs its keyword repeated per declarator, which no declarative edit can write
fix_steps: Move each `require()` declarator into its own `const` statement, and the other values into theirs.

rules.title: No new require(...)
rules.fix_reason: `new require(x)` and `new (require(x))()` call different functions; the rewrite is what was meant, not what runs now

rules.title: Join paths with path.join, not +
rules.fix_reason: the fix calls `path`, which the file may need to import

example.do:
const path = require("path");
const config = path.join(__dirname, "/config.json");

rules.title: No process.env outside the config module
rules.fix_reason: reading the environment in one place means adding a config module and changing every reader to use it
fix_steps: Read the variable once in the config module, validate it there, and export it.
Import the value from that module here.

rules.title: No process.exit()
rules.fix_reason: how to end the program cleanly depends on what is still running
fix_steps: Set `process.exitCode` and let the program finish, or throw an error the caller handles.

rules.title: No synchronous *Sync calls
rules.fix_reason: the async form returns a promise or takes a callback, so the calling code has to become async
fix_steps: Call the promise form (`fs.promises.readFile`, `await`) or the callback form instead, and make the caller async.
In a CLI or build script where blocking is fine, keep it and exclude the file from the rule.

rules.title: No await at the top level of a module
rules.fix_reason: moving the await into a function changes when the module finishes loading and what its importers see
fix_steps: Wrap the top-level work in an exported async function (`export async function init()`) that importers call.
In an entry script, use `main().catch(...)` with an `async function main()`.

example.dont:
const config = await loadConfig();
export default config;

rules.title: Published files import only what is published
rules.fix_reason: whether to publish the file, move the dependency or move the code is the package owner's choice
fix_steps: Add the imported file to `files` in the nearest `package.json`, move the package from `devDependencies` to `dependencies`, or move the import out of the published code.
A type-only import is not reported: it is erased from the published JavaScript.

rules.title: Published files require only what is published
rules.fix_reason: whether to publish the file, move the dependency or move the code is the package owner's choice
fix_steps: Add the required file to `files` in the nearest `package.json`, move the package from `devDependencies` to `dependencies`, or move the `require()` out of the published code.

rules.title: Use the global Buffer
rules.fix_reason: a bundler for the browser may resolve `buffer` to a polyfill package rather than Node's built-in, which the global is not

example.dont:
const { Buffer } = require("buffer");
const bytes = Buffer.from("hi");

rules.title: Use the global console
rules.fix_reason: a bundler for the browser may resolve `console` to a polyfill package rather than Node's built-in, which the global is not

rules.title: Use the global crypto
rules.fix_reason: a bundler for the browser may resolve `crypto` to a polyfill package rather than Node's built-in, which the global is not

example.dont:
const { webcrypto: crypto } = require("crypto");
const id = crypto.randomUUID();

rules.title: Use the global process
rules.fix_reason: a bundler for the browser may resolve `process` to a polyfill package rather than Node's built-in, which the global is not

rules.title: Use the global TextDecoder
rules.fix_reason: a bundler for the browser may resolve `util` to a polyfill package rather than Node's built-in, which the global is not

example.dont:
const { TextDecoder } = require("util");
const text = new TextDecoder().decode(bytes);

rules.title: Use the global TextEncoder
rules.fix_reason: a bundler for the browser may resolve `util` to a polyfill package rather than Node's built-in, which the global is not

example.dont:
const { TextEncoder } = require("util");
const bytes = new TextEncoder().encode(text);

rules.title: Use the global timer functions
rules.fix_reason: a bundler for the browser may resolve `timers` to a polyfill package rather than Node's built-in, which the global is not

rules.title: Use the global URL
rules.fix_reason: a bundler for the browser may resolve `url` to a polyfill package rather than Node's built-in, which the global is not

example.dont:
const { URL } = require("url");
const home = new URL("https://example.com");

rules.title: Use the global URLSearchParams
rules.fix_reason: a bundler for the browser may resolve `url` to a polyfill package rather than Node's built-in, which the global is not

example.dont:
import { URLSearchParams } from "url";
const q = new URLSearchParams("a=1");

rules.title: Import assert/strict
rules.fix_reason: in strict mode `assert.equal` and `assert.deepEqual` compare with `===` and stricter deep equality, so a passing check can start failing

rules.title: Import built-in modules with node:
rules.fix_reason: Node resolves `fs` and `node:fs` to the same built-in module

example.dont:
import { readFile } from "fs/promises";
const path = require("path");
example.do:
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
const path = require("node:path");

rules.title: Use the promise API of dns
rules.fix_reason: a callback becomes an awaited promise, so the caller has to become async and handle errors with try/catch
fix_steps: Import the function from `dns/promises` (or use `dns.promises`) and `await` it.
Move the callback body after the `await`, and its error branch into a `catch`.

rules.title: Use the promise API of fs
rules.fix_reason: a callback becomes an awaited promise, so the caller has to become async and handle errors with try/catch
fix_steps: Import the function from `fs/promises` (or use `fs.promises`) and `await` it.
Move the callback body after the `await`, and its error branch into a `catch`.

rules.title: No deprecated NumPy functions
rules.fix_reason: each has its own replacement name
fix_steps: Use `np.round`, `np.prod`, `np.cumprod`, `np.any` or `np.all`.

example.dont:
import numpy as np
t = np.product(xs)
example.do:
import numpy as np
t = np.prod(xs)

rules.title: Builtins, not NumPy's removed type aliases
rules.fix_reason: the builtin is what the alias meant; review a use that relied on NumPy's own type

example.dont:
import numpy as np
x = np.zeros(3, dtype=np.int)
example.do:
import numpy as np
x = np.zeros(3, dtype=int)

rules.title: A Generator, not np.random's legacy functions
rules.fix_reason: moving to a `Generator` means creating one and passing it where it is needed
fix_steps: Create `rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)` and call `rng.normal(...)` (and so on) on it.

example.dont:
import numpy as np
x = np.random.normal(size=3)
example.do:
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
x = rng.normal(size=3)

rules.title: No names NumPy 2 removed
rules.fix_reason: each removed name has its own replacement, given in the NumPy 2 migration guide
fix_steps: Use the replacement the NumPy 2 migration guide names (for example `np.inf` for `np.Inf`, `np.float64` for `np.float_`, `np.isin` for `np.in1d`).

example.dont:
import numpy as np
x = np.NaN
example.do:
import numpy as np
x = np.nan

rules.title: No nunique() to test a constant series
rules.fix_reason: the faster check is written by hand
fix_steps: Write `s.iloc[0] == s` and `.all()` (mind empty series and NaN).

example.dont:
import pandas as pd
flat = s.nunique() == 1
example.do:
import pandas as pd
flat = (s.iloc[0] == s).all()

rules.title: .loc, not .at
rules.fix_reason: `.loc` returns more than one value where `.at` would fail; confirm the lookup

example.dont:
import pandas as pd
v = df.at[0, 'a']
example.do:
import pandas as pd
v = df.loc[0, 'a']

rules.title: .iloc, not .iat
rules.fix_reason: `.iloc` returns more than one value where `.iat` would fail; confirm the lookup

example.dont:
import pandas as pd
v = df.iat[0, 1]
example.do:
import pandas as pd
v = df.iloc[0, 1]

rules.title: .isna, not .isnull
rules.fix_reason: the receiver may not be a pandas object; confirm before renaming

example.dont:
import pandas as pd
missing = df.isnull()
example.do:
import pandas as pd
missing = df.isna()

rules.title: No .ix
rules.fix_reason: `.loc` (labels) or `.iloc` (positions) depends on what the index holds: both are offered

example.dont:
import pandas as pd
row = df.ix[0]
example.do:
import pandas as pd
row = df.iloc[0]

rules.title: .notna, not .notnull
rules.fix_reason: the receiver may not be a pandas object; confirm before renaming

example.dont:
import pandas as pd
ok = df.notnull()
example.do:
import pandas as pd
ok = df.notna()

rules.title: pivot_table, not pivot or unstack
rules.fix_reason: `pivot_table` needs an aggregation function the author chooses
fix_steps: Rewrite as `pivot_table(index=…, columns=…, values=…, aggfunc=…)`.

example.dont:
import pandas as pd
wide = df.pivot(index='d', columns='k', values='v')
example.do:
import pandas as pd
wide = df.pivot_table(index='d', columns='k', values='v', aggfunc='sum')

rules.title: read_csv, not read_table
rules.fix_reason: the separator argument has to be added
fix_steps: Call `pd.read_csv(path, sep='\t')`.

example.dont:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_table('a.tsv')
example.do:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('a.tsv', sep='\t')

rules.title: melt, not stack
rules.fix_reason: `melt` takes different arguments, chosen by the author
fix_steps: Rewrite with `.melt(id_vars=…, value_vars=…)`.

example.dont:
import pandas as pd
long = df.stack()
example.do:
import pandas as pd
long = df.melt(id_vars=['d'])

rules.title: .to_numpy, not .values
rules.fix_reason: the receiver may be a dict-like whose `.values` is right; confirm before replacing

example.dont:
import pandas as pd
arr = df['a'].values
example.do:
import pandas as pd
arr = df['a'].to_numpy()

rules.title: No inplace=True
rules.fix_reason: the call must become an assignment of its result, which changes the statement
fix_steps: Remove `inplace=True` and assign the result: `df = df.dropna()`.

example.do:
import pandas as pd
df = df.dropna()

rules.title: df.merge, not pd.merge
rules.fix_reason: `a.merge(b)` needs `a` to be a DataFrame, where `pd.merge` also takes a named Series; review the receiver

example.dont:
import pandas as pd
out = pd.merge(a, b, on='id')
example.do:
import pandas as pd
out = a.merge(b, on='id')

rules.title: An abstract base class has an abstract method
rules.fix_reason: which methods subclasses must provide is a design decision
fix_steps: Mark the methods subclasses must override with `@abstractmethod`, or
drop `ABC` if the class isn't meant to be abstract.

rules.title: annotationlib, not __dict__['__annotations__']
rules.fix_reason: `inspect.get_annotations` evaluates lazily-defined annotations the dict lookup did not

rules.title: No classes named `l`, `O` or `I`
rules.fix_reason: the new name is the author's choice, and other modules may use the old one
fix_steps: Rename the class.
Update its uses, here and in modules that import it.

rules.title: No functions named `l`, `O` or `I`
rules.fix_reason: the new name is the author's choice, and other modules may use the old one
fix_steps: Rename the function.
Update its callers, here and in modules that import it.

rules.title: No variables named `l`, `O` or `I`
rules.fix_reason: the new name is the author's choice
fix_steps: Rename the variable to a descriptive name.
Update its uses.

example.dont:
class A:
    def __eq__(self, other: Any) -> bool: ...
example.do:
class A:
    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool: ...

rules.title: Don't `assert False`
rules.fix_reason: the check now also runs under `python -O`, where the assert was skipped

rules.title: No assert on a string
rules.fix_reason: the condition that was meant is the author's
fix_steps: Write the condition, and pass the string as the message: `assert cond, "..."`.

rules.title: Tests don't expect a bare `Exception`
rules.fix_reason: the exception the test expects has to be named by its author
fix_steps: Name the specific exception the code should raise.
With `pytest.raises`, add `match=` if the class can't be narrowed.

rules.title: `assert` doesn't test a tuple
rules.fix_reason: removing the parentheses turns a no-op into a check that can now fail
fix_steps: Remove the parentheses so the message becomes the assert's second operand.

rules.title: No print() as an assert message
Simple values only in stub assignments
No walrus inside assert
rules.fix_reason: the binding moves to its own statement before the assert
fix_steps: Bind the name on its own line before the assert, then assert on the name.

rules.title: Don't assign to `os.environ`
rules.fix_reason: whether to clear the environment first or only update it needs a person
fix_steps: Update `os.environ` item by item (`os.environ[key] = value`), clearing it first if that was meant.

rules.title: Keep a reference to every asyncio task
rules.fix_reason: the name to keep the task under, and where it is awaited, are the author's
fix_steps: Assign the task to a name or add it to a set kept for the program's life, and await it or discard it when it completes.

example.do:
async def main():
    task = asyncio.create_task(work())
    await task

rules.title: No await outside an async function
rules.fix_reason: making the function async changes every caller
fix_steps: Make the function `async def` and await it at its callers.

example.do:
async def fetch():
    return await client.get()

rules.title: A classmethod's first parameter is cls
rules.fix_reason: the parameter and its uses in the method are renamed

rules.title: Docstrings use triple double quotes
rules.fix_reason: auto when the docstring holds no double quote, so changing the delimiters cannot end it early

rules.title: No made-up dunder method names
rules.fix_reason: the intended name is the author's
fix_steps: Rename it to the special method you meant, or drop the double underscores.

rules.title: A metaclass classmethod's first parameter is mcs
rules.fix_reason: the parameter and its uses in the method are renamed

rules.title: A metaclass method's first parameter is cls
rules.fix_reason: the parameter and its uses in the method are renamed

rules.title: open() takes a valid mode
rules.fix_reason: which mode was meant is the author's
fix_steps: Use a valid mode such as `"r"`, `"w"`, `"rb"` or `"a+"`.

rules.title: A staticmethod takes no self
rules.fix_reason: whether it should be an instance method or the parameter renamed is the author's
fix_steps: Remove `@staticmethod` if the method needs the instance, or rename the parameter.

rules.title: % formats use valid conversion characters
rules.fix_reason: which conversion was meant is the author's
fix_steps: Use a valid conversion such as `%s`, `%d` or `%f`; write `%%` for a literal percent.

rules.title: Thread(target=f), not Thread(f)
rules.fix_reason: the function becomes the `target`, which is what was meant; it was the `group` argument

rules.title: `itertools.batched()` says `strict=`
rules.fix_reason: `strict=` exists only from Python 3.13, and codelaw cannot tell which Python the code runs on: on an older one the added keyword raises `TypeError`

target_version.description: the oldest Python the code supports; below 3.13 the rule is off

rules.title: No bidirectional control characters
rules.fix_reason: removing the character could hide what the code was made to look like; a person must read it
fix_steps: Remove the character, and check the code does what it looks like it does.

rules.title: except (A, B), not except A or B
rules.fix_reason: the handler then also catches `B`, which `A or B` never did

rules.title: int.bit_count(), not bin(x).count('1')
rules.fix_reason: `bit_count` needs Python 3.10 and an int

rules.title: noqa names its rule codes
rules.fix_reason: the codes to name are the linter's, not in the source
fix_steps: Write the codes the linter reports on the line: `# noqa: E501`.

ignore_names.description: a regular expression; functions named like this are exempt

fix_steps: Find a branch that decides one thing (a chain of `elif` over a kind, a run of `if`s that validate input) and extract it into a well-named function that returns the result.
Replace a long `if`/`elif` chain on one value with a dictionary of handlers, or a `match` that calls one function per case.
Return early on the guard cases so the main path has fewer nested branches.

rules.title: Every feature flag read is registered, with an owner and a date it goes
rules.fix_reason: Keeping one branch of a flag removes the other branch's code; a person or agent accepts the diff.

presets.description: `[flags] presets`, for this rule only: the SDKs whose reads codelaw knows (launchdarkly, unleash, split, openfeature, growthbook, flagsmith)

accessors.description: `[flags] accessors`, for this rule only: calls with one `$NAME` slot that read a flag

inline.description: `[flags] inline`, for this rule only: `allow` or `registry-only`

warn_days.description: `[flags] warn_days`, for this rule only: how many days before `expires` a read warns

fix_steps: Unregistered: add the flag to `.codelaw/flags.toml`, or mark it above the read: `# codelaw-flag <name> expires YYYY-MM-DD owner @team`.

Expiring or expired: set `keep = "on"` or `"off"` on its entry and run `codelaw fix --unsafe`: an `if` or a conditional expression whose whole condition is the read keeps that branch, dedented. Elsewhere, keep the branch by hand.
When the flag has no read left, `codelaw fix` removes its registry entry (`data/flag-registry`).

example.do:
# .codelaw/flags.toml
[[flag]]
name = "new-checkout"
owner = "@payments"
expires = "2026-12-31"
keep = "on"
# app/checkout.py
def total(cart):
    return new_total(cart)

rules.title: An inline flag marker agrees with the registry

presets.description: `[flags] presets`, for this rule only: the SDKs whose reads codelaw knows (launchdarkly, unleash, split, openfeature, growthbook, flagsmith)

accessors.description: `[flags] accessors`, for this rule only: calls with one `$NAME` slot that read a flag

inline.description: `[flags] inline`, for this rule only: `allow` or `registry-only`

warn_days.description: `[flags] warn_days`, for this rule only: how many days before `expires` a read warns

fix_steps: Run `codelaw fix`: a marker that disagrees with the registry is rewritten to match it, and a marker of a flag with no read left is removed.

A flag marked in several places with different values: add one `[[flag]]` entry for it to `.codelaw/flags.toml` with the values that are right, and delete the markers (or let `codelaw fix` rewrite them).
An unreadable marker: write it as `codelaw-flag <name> expires YYYY-MM-DD [owner …] [ticket …] [keep on|off] [reason …]`.

example.dont:
# .codelaw/flags.toml
[[flag]]
name = "beta"
owner = "@web"
expires = "2027-02-28"
# src/beta.py
# codelaw-flag beta expires 2027-01-31 owner @web
ON = is_feature_on("beta")
example.do:
# .codelaw/flags.toml
[[flag]]
name = "beta"
owner = "@web"
expires = "2027-02-28"
# src/beta.py
# codelaw-flag beta expires 2027-02-28 owner @web
ON = is_feature_on("beta")

target_version.description: the oldest Python the code supports; below 3.14 the rule is off

rules.title: math.pi, not 3.14159
rules.fix_reason: the constant is more precise than the literal, so results can change in the last digits

rules.title: Blocks nest no deeper than a maximum
rules.fix_reason: flattening nested blocks changes the function's structure; which guard to invert or which block to extract is the author's call

max.description: the most blocks that may nest inside one another in a function

fix_steps: Turn a guard into an early `return`, `continue` or `raise`, so the rest of the function sits one level up.
Extract the body of the innermost block into a well-named function.
Join a nested pair of `if`s with `and`, or flatten a `with` pair into one `with a, b:`.

rules.title: A module stays under a maximum number of lines
rules.fix_reason: splitting a module changes its structure; which names belong together is the author's call

max.description: the most lines a module may have

skip_comments.description: lines that hold only a comment do not count

fix_steps: Find a block inside the function that does one thing (a loop body, a branch, a run of statements that build one value).

ignore_names.description: a regular expression; parameters named like this do not count

rules.dont: def create_order(customer, items, coupon, address, note, gift):
fix_steps: Group the parameters that belong together into a dataclass or a `TypedDict`: `create_order(Order(customer, items, coupon, address, note, gift))`.
Or make the rarely used ones keyword-only with a bare `*`, and set `max_positional` to cap how many a caller passes by position.
If the signature is not yours to change, exempt it: an `@override` and an `@overload` stub already are.

max.description: the most lines one component may span

ignore_names.description: a regular expression; components named like this are exempt

fix_steps: Find a block of markup with its own name (a row, a header, a modal) and move it into a component of its own, passing in what it reads as props.
Move state and effects that belong to one part into a custom hook (`useTableSort`).
If the component is long on purpose, name it in `ignore_names`, or freeze it with `codelaw baseline add --rule react/component-max-lines`.

rules.title: Every default prop is a declared prop
rules.fix_reason: value: either the prop is declared, or the default is removed — which one is the author's
fix_steps: Declare the prop in `propTypes`, or remove the default if nothing reads it.

rules.title: Props and state are destructured
rules.fix_reason: restructure: a destructuring is written at the top of the component and every access is renamed, which a single edit cannot build
fix_steps: Write `const { … } = props;` (or `this.props`) at the top of the component, and use the names.

rules.title: A component passed to memo or forwardRef has a name
rules.fix_reason: the name is the author's choice
fix_steps: Pass a named function: `memo(function Card(props) { … })`.
Or set `Card.displayName = "Card"`.

rules.title: Errors in children are caught by an Error Boundary, not try/catch
rules.fix_reason: an Error Boundary is a component to add above this one, with its own fallback
fix_steps: Remove the `try`/`catch` around the JSX or the `use(…)` call.
Wrap the component's children (or the component, where it is used) in an Error Boundary with a fallback.

rules.title: Effect and memo dependency lists name every value they read
rules.fix_reason: adding a dependency can make an effect run more often

rules.title: No className or style on a component
rules.fix_reason: restructure: the styling moves into the component, which then takes a narrower prop
fix_steps: Move the styling into the component.
Give it a prop that names what varies (`variant="primary"`) and pass that instead.

rules.title: No prop the project forbids on DOM elements
rules.fix_reason: what replaces the prop is the project's convention, which the code doesn't hold

forbid.description: prop names DOM elements may not take

fix_steps: Remove the prop, or use the component the project provides.

rules.title: No element the project forbids
rules.fix_reason: which element replaces it is the project's convention, which the code doesn't hold

forbid.description: element or component names that may not be used

fix_steps: Use the component the project provides.

rules.title: No reading another component's propTypes
rules.fix_reason: restructure: the shape is exported from where it's defined and imported here
fix_steps: Export the prop shape from the component's module and import it where it's needed.

rules.title: No PropTypes.any, array or object
rules.fix_reason: value: the precise type — `arrayOf(…)`, `shape({…})` — is the author's
fix_steps: Use `PropTypes.arrayOf(…)`, `PropTypes.shape({…})` or `PropTypes.objectOf(…)` with the real element type.

rules.title: A forwardRef callback takes the ref
rules.fix_reason: adding the `ref` parameter is what the wrapper is for, but the author still has to attach it, or drop `forwardRef` instead

rules.title: Named components are function declarations
rules.fix_reason: restructure: the arrow is rewritten as a declaration, with its body, its type annotation and its export
fix_steps: Rewrite `const $N = (props) => …` as `function $N(props) { return …; }`, keeping the export.

rules.title: Render doesn't change module-level or global values
rules.fix_reason: where the change belongs — state, a ref, an effect, an event — depends on what the value is for
fix_steps: If the value belongs to the component, keep it in state or a ref.
If it must change outside React, change it in an effect or an event handler.

rules.title: Functions that call hooks are named use…
rules.fix_reason: every caller of the function must be renamed too
fix_steps: Rename the function to start with `use` (e.g. `loadUser` → `useUser`).
Rename its callers.

rules.title: useState is destructured as [value, setValue]
rules.fix_reason: value: the names are the author's; a template cannot recase the value's name into the setter's
fix_steps: Write `const [thing, setThing] = useState(…)`.

rules.title: An <iframe> has a sandbox
rules.fix_reason: an empty `sandbox` blocks scripts, forms and same-origin access in the frame, which a page that needs them must loosen by name

rules.title: Props and state are never mutated
rules.fix_reason: restructure: the change becomes a new value — a copy passed to the state setter, or a callback to the parent that owns the prop
fix_steps: Build a new value (`[...items, item]`, `{ ...user, name }`) and pass it to the state setter.
For a prop, call a callback the parent passes so the owner makes the change.

rules.title: No library API that defeats memoisation
rules.fix_reason: restructure: the component either opts out of compilation or reads the value through the library's memo-safe API
fix_steps: Add the `"use no memo"` directive to the component, or use the library's memo-safe API (`useWatch` for React Hook Form).

rules.title: A true prop is written bare
No inline element glued to text across a line break
rules.fix_reason: value: whether the words were meant to run together is the author's; a `{" "}` changes the rendered text
fix_steps: Put `{" "}` where a space is meant, or join the lines if no space is.

rules.title: No braces around a plain string prop
JSX lives in .jsx and .tsx files
rules.fix_reason: restructure: the file is renamed, and every import of it follows
fix_steps: Rename the file to `.jsx`.
Update the imports that name the extension.

rules.title: Handlers are named handle…, handler props on…
rules.fix_reason: value: the new method name is the author's
fix_steps: Rename the method to `handle<Event>`, or the prop to `on<Event>`, so the two prefixes match.

rules.title: Elements in an array or a map() callback have a key
rules.fix_reason: the key must be a stable identity of the item, which only the author knows
fix_steps: Give the element a `key` that identifies the item, such as its id.
Avoid the array index if items can be reordered or removed.

rules.title: No new function in a JSX prop
rules.fix_reason: restructure: the function moves out of render, into a method or a `useCallback` with its dependencies
fix_steps: Define the handler once: a class method, or a `useCallback` in a function component.
Pass it by name.

rules.title: No comment syntax as text inside JSX
rules.fix_reason: whether the text is a comment or content needs the author
fix_steps: Wrap the comment in braces: `{/* … */}`.

rules.title: A context value is not rebuilt on every render
rules.fix_reason: restructure: the value is memoised with `useMemo` (or hoisted), and its dependencies are the author's
fix_steps: Wrap the value in `useMemo` with its dependencies, or hoist it out of the component if it never changes.

rules.title: No prop given twice on one element
rules.fix_reason: which value should win needs the author
fix_steps: Keep the value that is right and remove the other.

rules.title: No JSX element built in a component's prop
rules.fix_reason: hoisting or memoising the element moves code out of the render
fix_steps: Hoist the element to a constant, or memoise it.

rules.title: No && that can render 0 or ""
rules.fix_reason: a ternary renders nothing where `&&` rendered `0` or `""`, which is the intent but is a visible change

rules.title: No bare text in JSX
rules.fix_reason: value: the text moves into the project's message catalogue under a key the author chooses
fix_steps: Add the text to the project's message catalogue under a key.
Render it with the project's translation call, e.g. `{t("save")}`.

rules.title: No array literal in a component's prop
rules.fix_reason: hoisting or memoising the array moves code out of the render
fix_steps: Hoist the array to a constant, or memoise it.

rules.title: No object literal in a component's prop
rules.fix_reason: hoisting or memoising the object moves code out of the render
fix_steps: Hoist the object to a constant, or memoise it.

example.do:
const center = { x: 0 };
const e = <Map center={center} />;

rules.title: No javascript: URLs in JSX
rules.fix_reason: security: the code the URL runs has to become a real handler
fix_steps: Move the code into an `onClick` handler.
Give the link a real `href`, or make it a `<button type="button">`.

rules.title: Links that open a new tab set rel="noreferrer"
Components used in JSX are declared
rules.fix_reason: the right import is the author's to choose
fix_steps: Import the component, or declare it, or correct the name.

example.do:
import { Header } from "./header";
export const App = () => <Header />;

rules.title: No fragment around a single element
Component names are PascalCase
rules.fix_reason: value: the new name is the author's, and every import of the component follows it
fix_steps: Rename the component to PascalCase (`UserCard`) where it's defined and everywhere it's imported.

rules.title: One object is not spread twice into a JSX element
rules.fix_reason: the later spread wins for every key it sets, so removing it can change a prop set between the two

rules.title: No spread props in JSX
rules.fix_reason: restructure: each prop the spread carried is named, which needs the set the author means to pass
fix_steps: List the props the element needs by name.

rules.title: JSX props are in alphabetical order
rules.fix_reason: reordering props reorders the evaluation of their values, and a later duplicate prop wins, so the order can matter
fix_steps: Sort the props.

rules.title: JSX elements nest no deeper than a maximum
rules.fix_reason: moving a nested part into a component means choosing its name and its props; that is the author's call

max.description: the most JSX elements that may nest inside one another

fix_steps: Take the subtree that starts at the reported element and move it into a component with a name that says what it is (`<ProfileMenu />`).
Pass in what the subtree reads as props.
A wrapper `<div>` that only carries a class can often be a prop on its child, or go away.

rules.title: A React component takes at most a maximum number of props
rules.fix_reason: grouping props changes the component's interface and every place that renders it; which props belong together is the author's call

max.description: the most props one component may take

ignore_names.description: a regular expression; components named like this are exempt

rules.dont: function Row({ id, name, email, phone }) {
fix_steps: Group props that always travel together into one object prop (`user={user}` instead of `id`, `name`, `email`).
Pass children instead of a prop per slot (`<Card><Header /></Card>`).
Split the component if its props fall into two sets used by different parts.
If the component is wide on purpose, name it in `ignore_names`, or freeze it with `codelaw baseline add --rule react/max-props`.

rules.title: Effect dependencies are stable values
rules.fix_reason: restructure: the value is wrapped in `useMemo` or `useCallback`, or moved inside the effect, with its own dependencies
fix_steps: Move `$D` inside the effect, or wrap it in `useMemo` / `useCallback` with its dependencies.

rules.title: setState does not read this.state
rules.fix_reason: restructure: the update becomes an updater function, `setState((state) => …)`, which reads its own state
fix_steps: Pass a function: `this.setState((state) => ({ count: state.count + 1 }))`.

rules.title: No inline elements that touch
rules.fix_reason: a space between the elements changes what is rendered
fix_steps: Add the space or text that was meant between them.

rules.title: No array index as a key
rules.fix_reason: value: a stable key comes from the item's data (an id), which only the author knows
fix_steps: Use a stable id from the item as the key: `key={item.id}`.

rules.title: Lifecycle methods are methods, not arrow fields
Children are passed as children, not as a prop
rules.fix_reason: moving the children changes the element's shape by hand
fix_steps: Move the value between the opening and closing tags.

rules.title: No `cloneElement`
rules.fix_reason: replacing a clone with props or a render function changes the component's API
fix_steps: Pass the props explicitly, or take a render function.

rules.title: No React context: no createContext, no useContext
rules.fix_reason: what replaces the context — props, a store, a module — is the team's design choice

use_instead.default: props or the app's state store
use_instead.description: what the codebase uses instead of context, named in the message

fix_steps: Pass the value another way — props, or the app's state store (the `use_instead` option names the team's choice) — and delete the `createContext` / `useContext` call.

If the use predates the rule, grandfather it instead: `codelaw baseline add --rule react/no-context --warn-from <today> --on-touch keep --reason "legacy context, grandfathered"` — today's uses then warn and new ones fail.

example.dont:
import { createContext } from 'react';

export const ThemeContext = createContext('light');

rules.title: No dangerouslySetInnerHTML together with children
rules.fix_reason: which content the element should have needs the author
fix_steps: Keep either the HTML or the children, not both.

rules.title: No deprecated React APIs
rules.fix_reason: each deprecated API has its own replacement
fix_steps: Replace `ReactDOM.render` with `createRoot(el).render(…)` and `hydrate` with `hydrateRoot`.
Rename legacy lifecycles to their `UNSAFE_` names, or move their work to `componentDidMount`/`componentDidUpdate`.
Use the `prop-types` package instead of `React.PropTypes`.

rules.title: No effect that only copies a value into state
rules.fix_reason: restructure: the derived value is computed during render and the state and the effect are deleted
fix_steps: Delete the state and the effect.
Compute the value in the component body: `const fullName = first + " " + last;` (with `useMemo` if it is expensive).

rules.title: No setState in componentDidMount
rules.fix_reason: restructure: the state is derived in render, or the update moves to a handler
fix_steps: Compute the value in `render` from props and state instead of storing it, or move the update into an event handler.

rules.title: No setState in componentDidUpdate
rules.fix_reason: restructure: the state is derived in render, or the update moves to a handler
fix_steps: Compute the value in `render` from props and state instead of storing it, or move the update into an event handler.

rules.title: No assigning to this.state outside the constructor
rules.fix_reason: the update has to be rewritten as a `setState` call
fix_steps: Replace the assignment with `this.setState(…)`; use the updater form when the new state depends on the old.

rules.title: No findDOMNode
rules.fix_reason: a ref has to be attached to the right element by hand
fix_steps: Attach a ref to the element you need (`ref={this.ref}`).
Read `ref.current` instead of calling `findDOMNode`.

rules.title: rel holds only valid link types
rules.fix_reason: value: which link type was meant is the author's
fix_steps: Correct or remove each unknown token; see the HTML standard's list of link types.

rules.title: No this.isMounted()
rules.fix_reason: the callback has to be cancelled where it starts
fix_steps: Cancel pending work in `componentWillUnmount`.
Remove the `isMounted` check.

rules.title: One component per file
rules.fix_reason: restructure: the component moves to its own file
fix_steps: Move the component to its own file and import it.

rules.title: No namespaced element names
rules.fix_reason: value: the element needs a real component or tag name
fix_steps: Use the plain tag (`<circle>` inside `<svg>`) or a component.

rules.title: Components are not defined inside other components
rules.fix_reason: moving the component out means passing in the values it closed over as props
fix_steps: Move the component to the top level of the module.
Pass the values it read from the outer component as props.

rules.title: No object or function literal as a prop default
rules.fix_reason: restructure: the default is hoisted to a module-level constant, whose name is the author's
fix_steps: Define the default once at module level (`const NO_ITEMS = [];`) and use it: `{ items = NO_ITEMS }`.

rules.title: No `React.Children` utilities
rules.fix_reason: passing the data as props changes the component's API
fix_steps: Take the items as a prop and render them.

rules.title: No shouldComponentUpdate on a PureComponent
rules.fix_reason: removing the method falls back to PureComponent's shallow comparison, which may re-render where the custom check did not

rules.title: A ref's current value is not read or written during render
rules.fix_reason: moving the access into an effect or an event handler changes when it runs
fix_steps: Move the read or write into an effect, an event handler or another callback.
If the value is shown on screen, keep it in state instead of a ref.
If the ref is created lazily, initialise it inside `if (ref.current === null) { … }`.

rules.title: The return value of ReactDOM.render is not used
rules.fix_reason: code that used the instance needs a ref instead
fix_steps: Pass a ref to the root element and use it instead of the return value.

rules.title: No this.setState
rules.fix_reason: restructure: the state moves to a store or to a parent, which is an architecture choice
fix_steps: Move the state to the project's store (or a parent component) and pass it in as props.

rules.title: An effect doesn't set state synchronously
rules.fix_reason: whether to derive the value, lift the state or subscribe is a design choice
fix_steps: If the value can be computed from props or state, compute it during render and drop the state and the effect.
If it depends on a change of a prop, handle the event that changed the prop instead.
If it comes from an outside source, subscribe in the effect and set the state in the subscription's callback, or use `useSyncExternalStore`.

rules.title: State is not set on every render
rules.fix_reason: what the state should be instead — derived during render, or set in an event — is a design choice
fix_steps: If the value can be computed from props or other state, compute it during render instead of storing it.
If the state must follow a prop, set it only when the prop changes: keep the previous prop in state and compare, inside an `if`.
Otherwise set it where the change happens: an event handler, or an effect's subscription callback.

rules.title: No string refs
rules.fix_reason: the ref object has to be created where the component can reach it
fix_steps: Create a ref with `useRef` or `createRef`.
Pass it as `ref={…}` and read `.current`.

rules.title: No stray semicolon after a JSX element
rules.fix_reason: the semicolon is rendered as text; whether it was meant is the author's call
fix_steps: Delete the semicolon.

rules.title: An SVG has a title or is hidden
rules.fix_reason: the title is the author's, or the SVG is decorative and should be hidden — the author decides which
fix_steps: Add `<title>` with a short name as the SVG's first child, or `aria-hidden="true"` if it is decorative.

rules.title: No this in a function component
rules.fix_reason: restructure: what `this` was meant to reach — props, state, a ref — is passed in or held in a hook
fix_steps: Read `props` from the function's parameter; keep state in `useState` and refs in `useRef`.

rules.title: No miscased React class members
rules.fix_reason: value: the intended name is read off the message; there is no template that recases a name
fix_steps: Spell the name as React does: `propTypes`, `defaultProps`, `contextTypes`, `componentDidMount`, …
