rules.title: No bypassSecurityTrust call on a value that is not a literal
rules.fix_reason: whether the value needs to be trusted at all is a decision for the author
fix_steps: Bind the value (`[innerHTML]="body"`) and let Angular sanitize it: it keeps safe tags and drops scripts.
If an element must be trusted (a fixed SVG), pass a literal, or sanitize the value with a library first (`DOMPurify`) and add a comment that says why trust is needed.
Never trust a value that came from a request, a URL or a user.

rules.title: No HTML written to a native element or through Renderer2
rules.fix_reason: whether the value is text or markup is a decision for the author

sanitizers.description: functions whose result may reach the sink: a callee path (global) or { name, module }; `sanitizers_mode: replace` makes them the only ones that count

fix_steps: Bind the value in the template: `[innerText]="text"` for text, `[innerHTML]="html"` for markup that Angular sanitizes.
With `Renderer2`, use `setProperty(el, "textContent", value)` or `createText` and `appendChild`.
If markup is needed and trusted, sanitize it first (`DomSanitizer.sanitize(SecurityContext.HTML, value)`).

rules.title: NestJS CORS names its origins
rules.fix_reason: which origins may call the API is a decision for the author
fix_steps: Pass the origins that may call the API: `app.enableCors({ origin: ["https://app.example.com"] })`.
Keep `credentials: true` only with an explicit origin list.

example.do:
const app = await NestFactory.create(AppModule);
app.enableCors({ origin: ["https://app.example.com"], credentials: true });

rules.title: A NestJS controller has a guard
rules.fix_reason: which guard protects the route is a decision for the author
fix_steps: Add `@UseGuards(AuthGuard)` to the controller (or register `APP_GUARD` once for the app and mark public routes `@Public()`).
Add role checks (`@Roles("admin")` with a `RolesGuard`) where the route is not for every signed-in user.

rules.title: A NestJS sign-in controller is rate limited
rules.fix_reason: the limits that fit the route are a decision for the author
fix_steps: Install `@nestjs/throttler`, add `ThrottlerGuard` to the controller (or globally) and `@Throttle({ default: { limit: 5, ttl: 60000 } })` to the route.
Add a lock-out or a growing delay after repeated failures for one account, and log them.

rules.title: ValidationPipe has whitelist on
rules.fix_reason: a client that sends fields no DTO names starts getting them stripped, which can change what an endpoint does

rules.title: A Next.js server action validates its input
rules.fix_reason: the schema and the authorisation check are written by the author

validators.description: calls that check input, any one of which in the function counts: a callee path or { name, module }; `validators_mode: replace` makes yours the only ones that count

fix_steps: Parse the arguments with a schema (`zod`, `valibot`) at the top of the action and use the parsed value only.
Check the caller next: read the session and refuse when the user may not do this (`const session = await auth(); if (!session) throw …`).
Return a small, typed result; never return a database row whole.

rules.title: No request typed any
rules.fix_reason: the real shape of the request is known only to the author
fix_steps: Type the request: `Request<Params, ResBody, ReqBody, Query>` in Express, a DTO class in NestJS.
Validate the body at run time as well (see `sec-ts/no-unchecked-cast-of-input`): a type only describes what the code expects.

rules.title: No request schema that lets anything through
rules.fix_reason: a client that sends extra keys starts getting an error instead of having them kept; `z.any()` and class-validator's `validate` have no mechanical fix

rules.title: No $queryRawUnsafe or $executeRawUnsafe with a value that is not a literal
rules.fix_reason: a `${…}` in the template becomes a bound parameter, which a statement that used it for a table or column name cannot do; only `$queryRawUnsafe` with one template is rewritten
rules.dont: const rows = await prisma.$queryRawUnsafe(`SELECT * FROM "User" WHERE id = ${id}`);
rules.do: const rows = await prisma.$queryRaw`SELECT * FROM "User" WHERE id = ${id}`;

example.dont: const rows = await prisma.$queryRawUnsafe(`SELECT * FROM "User" WHERE id = ${id}`);
example.do: const rows = await prisma.$queryRaw`SELECT * FROM "User" WHERE id = ${id}`;

rules.title: No raw SQL fragment from a value in Drizzle, Kysely or MikroORM
rules.fix_reason: the statement and its values have to be separated by hand
rules.do: await db.execute(sql`select * from users where id = ${id}`);
fix_steps: Use the `sql` tagged template: each `${value}` becomes a parameter. `sql.raw` is for a fixed fragment you wrote, as a literal.
A table or column name that must vary is picked from an allow-list in code, then written with `sql.identifier(name)` (Drizzle) or `sql.id(name)` (Kysely).

example.do: await db.execute(sql`select * from users where id = ${id}`);

rules.title: No type error silenced on a line that holds a security sink
rules.fix_reason: what the right type is depends on the value
fix_steps: Fix the type instead: narrow the value, or convert it with a function that returns the type the sink wants.
If the sink really needs a value of another type, write a small typed helper for it and keep the cast inside the helper, with a comment that says why it is safe.

rules.title: No TypeORM query built from a template or concatenation
rules.fix_reason: the condition and its values have to be separated by hand
fix_steps: Write the condition with a named parameter (`"u.id = :id"`) and pass the values as the second argument: `.where("u.id = :id", { id })`.
For `repo.query`, use the driver's placeholders (`$1`, `?`) and an array of values.
A column or table name cannot be a parameter: take it from an allow-list in code.

rules.title: No type assertion on input that nothing has checked
rules.fix_reason: the schema that describes the input is written by the author

validators.description: calls that check input, any one of which in the function counts: a callee path or { name, module }; `validators_mode: replace` makes yours the only ones that count

fix_steps: Parse the value with a schema (`zod`, `valibot`, `ajv`) and use the parsed result, whose type is inferred from the schema.
In NestJS, take a DTO class with `class-validator` decorators and a `ValidationPipe`, not a cast.
For `JSON.parse`, check the shape of the result before it is used as `T`.

rules.title: A tRPC mutation is not public
rules.fix_reason: which procedure carries the auth middleware is named by the author
rules.dont: export const create = publicProcedure.input(schema).mutation(({ input }) => save(input));
fix_steps: Use `protectedProcedure` (one that runs the session check as middleware) for every mutation, and `.use(isAdmin)` where a role is needed.
If a mutation really is public (a contact form), leave `publicProcedure` and suppress this finding with a reason that says why, and rate-limit it.

example.dont: export const create = publicProcedure.input(schema).mutation(({ input }) => save(input));

rules.title: TypeORM does not synchronize the schema on start
rules.fix_reason: how the schema is changed instead (migrations) is a decision for the author
rules.dont: export const db = new DataSource({ type: "postgres", url, synchronize: true });
rules.do: export const db = new DataSource({ type: "postgres", url, migrations: ["dist/migrations/*.js"] });
fix_steps: Set `synchronize: false` (the default) and write migrations: `typeorm migration:generate`, then `migration:run` at deploy.
If it is only for a local database, set it from an environment variable that is never true in production.

example.dont: export const db = new DataSource({ type: "postgres", url, synchronize: true });
example.do: export const db = new DataSource({ type: "postgres", url, migrations: ["dist/migrations/*.js"] });

rules.title: A word is spelled one way across the project
rules.fix_reason: the spelling a project uses most is usually its house style, but a quotation, a product name or a file in the other locale may be right as it is
rules.dont: // The cancelled orders are listed below.
rules.do: // The canceled orders are listed below.
fix_steps: Run `codelaw fix --unsafe` to write the spelling the project uses most, or change the word by hand.
If the project means one locale, set `[spell] locale` and turn on `spell/locale-variant`, which fixes the other locale's spelling unattended.
For a quotation or a proper name (`Colour Science Ltd`), excuse the line: `// codelaw-ignore spell/inconsistent-term: <reason>`.

rules.title: No known typos in comments, docs and prose
rules.dont: // Retry until we recieve a response.
rules.do: // Retry until we receive a response.
fix_steps: Run `codelaw fix`: each typo becomes its correction.
For a word that is right where it stands (a product name, a quoted misspelling), excuse the line: `// codelaw-ignore spell/known-typo: <reason>`.

example.dont:
// Retry until we recieve a response.
throw new Error("Unexpected lenght of the header");
example.do:
// Retry until we receive a response.
throw new Error("Unexpected length of the header");

rules.title: No known typos in the names a file declares
fix_steps: Run `codelaw fix`: a file-local name is renamed at its declaration and every use.
For an exported name, a module-level name or a member, rename it with your editor's rename across the project, and keep the old name as a deprecated alias if other packages import it.
For a name that is right as it stands (a product name, a field another system defines), excuse the line: `// codelaw-ignore spell/known-typo-identifier: <reason>`.

rules.title: No known typos in keys, classes and ids
rules.fix_reason: other files read the name — the code that reads a key, the markup that uses a class, the link to an id — so renaming it here alone breaks them
fix_steps: Find every reader of the name: search the project for it (`git grep -n recieve_all`), including code that builds it from parts.
Rename it here and in every reader in one change; for a key or class published to other projects, accept both names for a release before removing the old one.
For a name that is right as it stands (a field another system defines), excuse the line: `# codelaw-ignore spell/known-typo-key: <reason>`.

rules.title: Prose is spelled in the project's locale

locale.description: `en-US` or `en-GB`: the locale whose spellings are right; read from `[spell] locale`, and the rule reports nothing while it is unset

fix_steps: Run `codelaw fix`: each word becomes the locale's spelling.
For a quotation or a proper name (`Colour Science Ltd`), excuse the line: `// codelaw-ignore spell/locale-variant: <reason>`, or add the word to `[spell] words`.

rules.title: No accepted word hides a typo
rules.fix_reason: only the team knows whether an accepted word is a real name or a misspelling it waved through
fix_steps: Search the project for the word (`git grep -n -i recieve`).
If it is a misspelling, fix it where it appears and take it out of `[spell] words`.
If it is right (a name that looks like a typo), keep it and excuse the line: `# codelaw-ignore spell/suspicious-word: <reason>`.

rules.title: Every word of prose is in a word list
rules.fix_reason: a word no list holds is often a real name, a product or a term of the trade; the nearest dictionary word is a guess the author confirms
fix_steps: If the word is misspelled, run `codelaw fix --unsafe` to take the first suggestion, or write the word the message names that you meant.
If the word is right (a name, a product, a term of your trade), add it to the root `codelaw.toml`: `[spell]` `words = ["kubectl"]`. `spell/suspicious-word` checks the list.
For a one-off, excuse the line: `// codelaw-ignore spell/unknown-word: <reason>`.

rules.title: A boolean @Prop defaults to false
rules.fix_reason: inverting the prop renames it for every user
fix_steps: Invert the prop's meaning so it defaults to `false` (e.g. `closable` → `hideClose`).
Update the component's markup users.

rules.title: A component tag doesn't use a reserved prefix
rules.fix_reason: renaming a tag changes every page that uses it
fix_steps: Choose a prefix of your own and rename the tag.
Update every usage of the element.

rules.title: No calls at a module's top level
rules.fix_reason: where the call should run instead — a function, a lifecycle method — needs the author

allow.description: functions that may be called at the top level; setting it replaces the default list

fix_steps: Move the call into the function, method or lifecycle hook (`componentWillLoad`, `connectedCallback`) that needs its effect.
If the call builds a value, export a function that builds it, or keep it in an `export const`.
If the call must run at load time, add the function's name to the `allow` option.

rules.title: Stencil decorators only inside @Component classes
rules.fix_reason: whether the class should be a component needs the author
fix_steps: Make the class a `@Component`, or remove the Stencil decorators.

rules.title: Every slot a component renders has a @slot tag, and every @slot tag a slot
rules.fix_reason: the slot's description, or whether it should exist, needs the author
fix_steps: For a slot reported as rendered without a tag, add `@slot <name> - <what it holds>` (or `@slot - <what it holds>` for the default slot) to the JSDoc above `@Component`.
For a tag reported as never rendered, remove the tag, or render the `<slot>` it describes.

rules.title: No hostData()
rules.fix_reason: the attributes move into `render()` by hand
fix_steps: Render a `<Host>` element in `render()` with the attributes `hostData()` returned.
Remove `hostData()`.

rules.title: @Method() members are public
rules.fix_reason: whether the method is public API needs the author
fix_steps: Remove `private`/`protected`, or remove `@Method()` if it isn't public API.

rules.title: @Watch watches a @Prop or @State
rules.fix_reason: which member was meant needs the author
fix_steps: Correct the name to the @Prop or @State it should watch, or remove the watcher.

rules.title: A component's own methods are private
A component's own fields are private
DOM events are handled in render(), not with @Listen
rules.fix_reason: the handler moves into the rendered markup by hand
fix_steps: Attach the handler in `render()` (e.g. `onClick={…}` on `<Host>`).
Remove the `@Listen`.

rules.title: @Prop() members are public
rules.fix_reason: whether the field is public API needs the author
fix_steps: Remove `private`/`protected`, or make it a `@State()` if it is internal.

rules.title: Public members have JSDoc
rules.fix_reason: the documentation text needs the author
rules.do: /** The heading shown at the top. */
fix_steps: Write a `/** … */` comment above the member saying what it is for.

rules.title: Public members don't reuse HTML element names
rules.fix_reason: renaming a public member changes every user
fix_steps: Rename the member.
Update its users.

rules.title: mutable: true only on props the component changes
rules.fix_reason: whether the component should change the prop needs the author
fix_steps: Remove `mutable: true` and make the prop `readonly`, or assign it where the component means to.

rules.title: Component tags start with the project's prefix
rules.fix_reason: renaming a tag changes every page that uses it

prefix.description: the prefix every tag must start with

fix_steps: Rename the tag to start with the project's prefix.
Update every usage of the element.

rules.title: Classes are written as Tailwind spells them
fix_steps: Write the class Tailwind's canonical way, as the finding names it.

rules.title: A negative arbitrary value keeps its minus inside the brackets
fix_steps: Drop the leading `-` and put it inside the brackets: `-m-[4px]` → `m-[-4px]`.

rules.title: The important modifier comes last
fix_steps: Move the `!` from the start of the utility to the end of the class.

rules.title: No arbitrary values
rules.fix_reason: the right theme value is the author's choice; the code holds only the arbitrary one
fix_steps: Pick the theme value closest to the intent (`w-[13px]` → `w-3` or `w-3.5`).
If the system needs the value, add it to the theme (`@theme { --spacing-… }`) and use its name.

rules.title: Classes are not joined with +
rules.fix_reason: a template literal converts its parts with String(); `+` with an object operand calls valueOf first
fix_steps: Write the chain as one template literal.
Or pass the parts to `cn(...)`/`clsx(...)` as separate arguments.

rules.title: No two classes set the same properties
rules.fix_reason: the losing class does nothing in Tailwind's own CSS, but a selector of the project's could still read it
fix_steps: Keep the class you mean and remove the other.

rules.title: No classes the project restricts
rules.fix_reason: removing a class changes how the element looks; a person accepts the diff

restrict.description: regular expressions, each matched against a whole class

fix_steps: Remove the class, or replace it with the one the project uses instead.

rules.title: Every class is one the project's Tailwind knows
rules.fix_reason: an unknown class may be styled by the project's own CSS or read by a script; removing it needs a person

ignore.description: regular expressions for the project's own classes, each matched against a whole class

fix_steps: Fix the typo, or remove the class.
If the project's CSS defines it, add a pattern for it to `ignore`.

rules.title: A query key is an array
rules.fix_reason: wrapping the key in an array changes its hash, so a key matched elsewhere in its old form stops matching
fix_steps: Wrap the key in an array: `queryKey: ['todos']`.

example.dont:
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';

useQuery({ queryKey: 'todos', queryFn: fetchTodos });
example.do:
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';

useQuery({ queryKey: ['todos'], queryFn: fetchTodos });

rules.title: A query key names every value its query function reads
rules.fix_reason: a new key entry changes which cache entry the query reads and writes

allowlist.description: `{ variables: [<name>…], types: [<type name>…] }`: values to leave out of the key, by name or by their declared type

rules.do: return useQuery({ queryKey: ['todo', id], queryFn: () => fetchTodo(id) });

rules.title: An infinite query's `queryFn` comes before its page-param callbacks
fix_steps: Move `queryFn` above `getPreviousPageParam` and `getNextPageParam`. The fix is offered only when every moved option is a function or a name, so the order nothing else runs in is kept.

rules.title: A mutation's `onMutate` comes before `onError` and `onSettled`
fix_steps: Move `onMutate` above `onError` and `onSettled`. The fix is offered only when every moved option is a function or a name.

rules.title: A `setQueryData` updater does not change the cached data in place
rules.fix_reason: the update has to be rewritten to build a new value
fix_steps: Return a new value built from the old one: `{ ...old, title }`, `[...old, item]`, `old.filter(…)`, `old.map(…)`.
For deep updates, build the copy with Immer's `produce(old, (draft) => { … })`, which is where an in-place change is correct.

rules.title: A query takes no option TanStack Query v5 removed
rules.fix_reason: each removed option is replaced by different code: an effect, `placeholderData`, `structuralSharing` or a hook argument
fix_steps: `onSuccess` / `onError` / `onSettled`: react to `data` or `error` where the query is rendered, move the work into the `queryFn`, or use the `QueryCache`'s global callbacks.
`keepPreviousData: true`: write `placeholderData: keepPreviousData`, importing `keepPreviousData` from TanStack Query, and read `isPlaceholderData` instead of `isPreviousData`.
`isDataEqual`: pass `structuralSharing: (old, next) => (equal(old, next) ? old : replaceEqualDeep(old, next))`.
`context`: pass the `QueryClient` as the hook's second argument.

rules.title: An option uses its TanStack Query v5 name
fix_steps: Rename the key. The fix is not offered when the object already has the new name too.

rules.title: No rest destructuring of a query result
rules.fix_reason: which fields the component needs is a choice only its author can make
rules.dont: const { data, ...rest } = useQuery({ queryKey: ['todos'], queryFn: fetchTodos });
rules.do: const { data, isPending } = useQuery({ queryKey: ['todos'], queryFn: fetchTodos });
fix_steps: Destructure the fields the component uses by name: `const { data, isPending } = useQuery(…)`.
Or keep the result whole (`const query = useQuery(…)`) and read `query.data` where it is used.

rules.title: A query hook's result is not a React hook dependency
rules.fix_reason: the fields to list depend on what the effect, callback or memo reads
fix_steps: Destructure the fields the hook reads: `const { mutate } = useMutation(…)`.
List those fields in the dependency array instead of the whole result.

rules.title: A suspense query takes no `enabled`, `placeholderData` or `throwOnError`
rules.fix_reason: removing `enabled` makes the query always run, and removing `placeholderData` shows the fallback during an update
fix_steps: `enabled`: render the component only when the query should run, or use `useQuery`.
`placeholderData`: wrap the update that changes the query key in `startTransition`.
`throwOnError`: throw `error` yourself when `!isFetching`, to send every error to the boundary.

rules.title: A query function returns its data
rules.fix_reason: what the query should return is the data the function fetches, which the author knows
fix_steps: Return the fetched data: `return res.json()`, or `return response.data`.
If the function only triggers work, it is a mutation: move it to `useMutation`'s `mutationFn`.

rules.title: A TanStack Query call takes one options object
rules.fix_reason: the positional arguments are moved into a new object, which changes the call's shape
fix_steps: Move the arguments into one object: `useQuery(key, fn, options)` becomes `useQuery({ queryKey: key, queryFn: fn, ...options })`. The fix is offered when the arguments' roles can be read off the call: an options object written in place, or a function written in place.

example.dont:
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';

useQuery(['todos'], fetchTodos, { staleTime: 5000 });
example.do:
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';

useQuery({ queryKey: ['todos'], queryFn: fetchTodos, staleTime: 5000 });

rules.title: The QueryClient is made once, not on every render
rules.fix_reason: the fix calls `React.useState` (or the imported `useState`), which must be in scope

rules.title: `.for` over `.each` in Vitest
rules.fix_reason: `.for` passes each row as one argument, so the callback's parameters change shape
fix_steps: Replace `.each` with `.for`.
Destructure the row in the callback's first parameter: `([a, b]) => …`.

rules.title: Test files named `*.test.*`
rules.fix_reason: renaming the file changes every path that names it
rules.do: export const add = (a, b) => a + b;
fix_steps: Rename the file from `<name>.spec.<ext>` to `<name>.test.<ext>`.

example.do: export const add = (a, b) => a + b;

rules.title: Every test asserts
rules.fix_reason: the assertion a test is missing is the author's to write
fix_steps: Add an `expect` on the result the test is about.
If the test only checks that nothing throws, say so: `expect(() => run()).not.toThrow()`.

rules.title: `vi.mock` and `vi.hoisted` at the top level
rules.fix_reason: the call already runs first; moving it changes nothing at run time but may move code the author placed for a reason

rules.title: At most five assertions in a test
rules.fix_reason: splitting the test decides which assertions belong together
rules.do: expect(u).toMatchObject({ a: 1, b: 2, c: 3, d: 4, e: 5, f: 6 });
fix_steps: Split the test into several, each asserting one behaviour.

rules.title: At most five nested `describe` blocks
rules.fix_reason: flattening the nesting moves tests between blocks and files
fix_steps: Merge levels that add no setup of their own, or move a deep group to its own file.

rules.title: No commented-out tests
rules.fix_reason: deleting the comment loses the test; restoring it may fail — the author decides which

rules.title: No `expect` inside a condition
rules.fix_reason: the test has to be split or its setup fixed so the assertion always runs; no edit can tell which
fix_steps: Split the test so each case sets up the state it asserts on, and assert unconditionally.
For an expected error, use `expect(() => …).toThrow()` or `await expect(p).rejects…` instead of `try`/`catch`.

rules.title: No conditional logic in a test
rules.fix_reason: each branch becomes its own test, with its own setup; how to split is the author's call
fix_steps: Write one test per branch, each with the setup that makes that branch happen.
Use `test.each` when the branches differ only in data.

rules.title: No tests declared inside a condition
rules.fix_reason: the condition becomes `test.skipIf`/`runIf` or a test of its own, which the author chooses
fix_steps: Replace `if (cond) { test(…) }` with `test.runIf(cond)(…)`, or `test.skipIf(!cond)(…)`.

rules.title: `jest.setTimeout` once, at the top of the file
rules.fix_reason: moving the call changes the timeout of the tests above it

rules.title: No `done` callback in tests and hooks
rules.fix_reason: the callback-style code becomes `async`/`await` or a returned promise, which changes the body's shape
fix_steps: Make the callback `async` and drop the parameter.
`await` the work; wrap a callback API in a `Promise` if it has no promise form.

rules.title: One hook of each kind per block
rules.fix_reason: merging two hooks means choosing the order of their statements
fix_steps: Move the second hook's statements into the first, in the order they should run.
Delete the second hook.

rules.title: No exports from a test file
rules.fix_reason: the exported code moves to a module of its own, and its importers change
fix_steps: Move the exported helper to its own module (`test-utils.ts`).
Import it from there in every test file that uses it.

rules.title: No setup and teardown hooks
rules.fix_reason: the hook's work moves into each test or a helper the tests call
fix_steps: Write a function that returns what the hook prepared.
Call it at the start of each test that needs it, and delete the hook.

rules.title: No two tests with one title
rules.fix_reason: a new title has to say what the second test checks
fix_steps: Rename one of the two to say what it checks that the other does not.
If they check the same thing, delete one.

example.dont:
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
it("t", () => {});

rules.title: No interpolation in an inline snapshot
rules.fix_reason: the snapshot has to hold the literal value; a property matcher replaces the dynamic part
fix_steps: Replace the dynamic part with a property matcher: `toMatchInlineSnapshot({ id: expect.any(String) }, `…`)`.
Or write the literal value.

rules.title: No inline snapshot longer than 50 lines
rules.fix_reason: what to assert instead of the whole value is the author's choice
fix_steps: Assert on the few fields the test is about (`toMatchObject`, `toHaveProperty`).
Or snapshot a smaller piece of the value.

example.dont:
test("big", () => {
  expect(page).toMatchInlineSnapshot(`  line 0

  line 28
  line 29
  line 30

  line 33
  line 34
  line 35
  line 36
  line 37
  line 38
  line 39
  line 40
  line 41
  line 42
  line 43
  line 44
  line 45
  line 46
  line 47
  line 48
  line 49
  line 50
  line 51
`);
});

rules.title: No imports from `__mocks__`
rules.fix_reason: the module is mocked with `jest.mock` and imported by its real path; the import changes shape
fix_steps: Import the module by its real path.
Call `jest.mock("<path>")` (or `vi.mock`) so the mock is used.

rules.title: No `jest` methods the project restricts
rules.fix_reason: what to use instead is the project's convention, named in its message
fix_steps: Replace the call with the project's convention.

rules.title: No matchers the project restricts
rules.fix_reason: what to use instead is the project's convention
fix_steps: Use the matcher the project prefers.

rules.title: No `vi` methods the project restricts
rules.fix_reason: what to use instead is the project's convention, named in its message
fix_steps: Replace the call with the project's convention.

rules.title: No `expect` outside a test or hook
rules.fix_reason: the assertion moves into a test, which needs a title
fix_steps: Move the assertion into a test (`test("…", () => { expect(…) })`) or a hook.

rules.title: No `return` from a test
rules.fix_reason: `await` needs the callback to be `async`, and a returned value that is not a promise is a mistake to remove
fix_steps: Make the callback `async`.
Replace `return <promise>` with `await <promise>`.

rules.title: No async wrapper around an awaited promise in `expect`
Every test asserts
rules.fix_reason: the assertion a test is missing is the author's to write
fix_steps: Add an `expect` on the result the test is about.
If the test only checks that nothing throws, say so: `expect(() => run()).not.toThrow()`.

rules.title: At most five assertions in a test
rules.fix_reason: splitting the test decides which assertions belong together
rules.do: expect(u).toMatchObject({ a: 1, b: 2, c: 3, d: 4, e: 5, f: 6 });
fix_steps: Split the test into several, each asserting one behaviour.

rules.title: At most five nested `describe` blocks
rules.fix_reason: flattening the nesting moves tests between blocks and files
fix_steps: Merge levels that add no setup of their own, or move a deep group to its own file.

rules.title: No `timeout` on an action
rules.fix_reason: dropping the timeout makes the action use the configured one, which may be shorter

rules.title: No commented-out tests
rules.fix_reason: deleting the comment loses the test; restoring it may fail — the author decides which

rules.title: No `expect` inside a condition
rules.fix_reason: the test has to be split or its setup fixed so the assertion always runs; no edit can tell which
fix_steps: Split the test so each case sets up the state it asserts on, and assert unconditionally.
For an expected error, use `expect(() => …).toThrow()` or `await expect(p).rejects…` instead of `try`/`catch`.

rules.title: No conditional logic in a test
rules.fix_reason: each branch becomes its own test, with its own setup; how to split is the author's call
fix_steps: Write one test per branch, each with the setup that makes that branch happen.
Use `test.each` when the branches differ only in data.

rules.title: One hook of each kind per block
rules.fix_reason: merging two hooks means choosing the order of their statements
fix_steps: Move the second hook's statements into the first, in the order they should run.
Delete the second hook.

rules.title: Locators, not element handles
rules.fix_reason: a locator is lazy and strict where a handle was resolved once, so later lines may behave differently

rules.title: No `$eval` and `$$eval`
rules.fix_reason: the evaluation becomes a locator assertion or `locator.evaluate`, which needs knowing what is checked
fix_steps: Replace `page.$eval(sel, fn)` with `page.locator(sel).evaluate(fn)`, or with a web-first assertion on the locator.

rules.title: No exports from a test file
rules.fix_reason: the exported code moves to a module of its own, and its importers change
fix_steps: Move the exported helper to its own module (`test-utils.ts`).
Import it from there in every test file that uses it.

rules.title: No `force: true` on actions
rules.fix_reason: without `force` the action waits for the element to be actionable, and may now time out

rules.title: No `getByTitle`
rules.fix_reason: the query becomes one by role or label, which needs knowing what the user perceives
fix_steps: Use `getByRole(…, { name })` or `getByLabel(…)` instead.

rules.title: No setup and teardown hooks
rules.fix_reason: the hook's work moves into each test or a helper the tests call
fix_steps: Write a function that returns what the hook prepared.
Call it at the start of each test that needs it, and delete the hook.

rules.title: No two tests with one title
rules.fix_reason: a new title has to say what the second test checks
fix_steps: Rename one of the two to say what it checks that the other does not.
If they check the same thing, delete one.

rules.title: No literal timeout values
rules.fix_reason: the named constant, and where it lives, are the author's choice
fix_steps: Declare the value once with a name (`const SLOW_API_MS = 10_000`) and use the name.

rules.title: No `test.step` inside a step
rules.fix_reason: flattening steps changes how the report groups them
fix_steps: Move the inner step out to the same level as its parent.

rules.title: No `networkidle`
rules.fix_reason: the wait becomes an assertion on what the page shows, which needs knowing what it waits for
fix_steps: Replace the wait with a web-first assertion on the element the test needs: `await expect(page.getByRole("table")).toBeVisible()`.

rules.title: No `first()`, `last()` and `nth()`
rules.fix_reason: a unique locator needs knowing what distinguishes the element
fix_steps: Add the distinguishing text, name or role to the locator, or `filter({ hasText })`.

rules.title: No `page.pause()` left in a test
rules.fix_reason: the call only stops for debugging; removing it is safe but the author may still be using it

rules.title: No CSS or XPath locators
rules.fix_reason: the locator becomes one by role, label or text, which needs knowing what the user sees
fix_steps: Replace it with `getByRole`, `getByLabel`, `getByText` or `getByTestId`.

rules.title: No locator methods the project restricts
rules.fix_reason: which locator to use instead is the project's convention
fix_steps: Use the locator the project prefers, usually `getByRole` or `getByLabel`.

rules.title: No matchers the project restricts
rules.fix_reason: what to use instead is the project's convention
fix_steps: Use the matcher the project prefers.

rules.title: No `getByRole` roles the project restricts
rules.fix_reason: the role that fits is the author's to choose
fix_steps: Locate the element by a meaningful role, or by its label.

rules.title: No `test.slow()`
rules.fix_reason: without it the test runs at the normal timeout and may now time out

rules.title: No `expect` outside a test or hook
rules.fix_reason: the assertion moves into a test, which needs a title
fix_steps: Move the assertion into a test (`test("…", () => { expect(…) })`) or a hook.

rules.title: No template literal as a test title
No `return` from a test
rules.fix_reason: `await` needs the callback to be `async`, and a returned value that is not a promise is a mistake to remove
fix_steps: Make the callback `async`.
Replace `return <promise>` with `await <promise>`.

rules.title: No assertion on a constant
rules.fix_reason: deleting the assertion is safe only if it was indeed left in by mistake

rules.title: No locator created and left unused
rules.fix_reason: what the locator was for — an action or an assertion — is the author's to write
fix_steps: Act on it (`.click()`), assert on it (`await expect(…).toBeVisible()`), or delete it.

rules.title: No `.not` where a matcher says it
No `waitForNavigation`
rules.fix_reason: the replacement assertion on the URL needs the URL the author expects; deleting the call is the suggested half
fix_steps: After the action, assert the destination: `await expect(page).toHaveURL("/next")`.

rules.title: No `waitForSelector`
rules.fix_reason: a locator's `waitFor` is strict where `waitForSelector` took the first match

rules.title: No fixed sleeps
rules.fix_reason: without the sleep the next line runs at once; it may need a web-first assertion in its place

rules.title: A test ends with an assertion
rules.fix_reason: what to assert after the last action is the author's to write
fix_steps: Add an assertion on the effect of the last statement, or move that statement before the last assertion.

rules.title: An equality matcher for an equality
rules.fix_reason: `toBe` compares with `Object.is`, not `===`: `NaN` and `-0` compare differently, so the author confirms the edit

rules.title: Hooks in the order they run
rules.fix_reason: reordering hooks moves their statements; the author checks nothing depends on the old order
fix_steps: Move the hook above the hooks that run after it.

rules.title: Hooks before the tests
rules.fix_reason: moving a hook above tests changes nothing at run time but the author places it
fix_steps: Move the hook above the first test of its block.

rules.title: Locator methods over `page` actions
rules.fix_reason: a locator is strict — it fails on more than one match where the page method took the first

rules.title: Test titles start in lower case
`toStrictEqual` over `toEqual`
rules.fix_reason: `toStrictEqual` also checks `undefined` properties, sparse arrays and class types, so an assertion that passed may now fail

rules.title: `toHaveCount` for a locator's count
rules.fix_reason: `toHaveCount` retries until the count matches, so an assertion that failed at once may now pass after waiting

rules.title: Web-first assertions over reading state
rules.fix_reason: the web-first matcher retries until it passes, so an assertion that failed at once may now pass after waiting

rules.title: Annotations give a reason
rules.fix_reason: the reason is the author's to write
fix_steps: Add the reason as the last argument: `test.fixme(true, "crashes on Safari, #123")`.

rules.title: Setup code in a hook
rules.fix_reason: the code moves into a `beforeAll` or `beforeEach`, chosen by when it must run
fix_steps: Wrap the statement in `beforeAll` (once) or `beforeEach` (per test).

rules.title: Soft assertions
rules.fix_reason: a soft assertion lets the test go on after a failure, which changes what runs after it

rules.title: Every test is tagged
rules.fix_reason: which tag fits the test is the author's choice
fix_steps: Add a tag: `test("…", { tag: "@smoke" }, async () => { … })`.

rules.title: `toPass` with a timeout
rules.fix_reason: how long the block may retry depends on what it waits for
fix_steps: Pass a timeout: `toPass({ timeout: 10_000 })`.

rules.title: `toThrow` names the error
rules.fix_reason: the expected message or error class is the author's to write
fix_steps: Pass the message, a regular expression or the error class: `toThrow("not found")`, `toThrow(NotFoundError)`.

rules.title: Tests inside a top-level `describe`
rules.fix_reason: wrapping the file's tests in a `describe` needs a title for it
fix_steps: Wrap the file's tests and hooks in `describe("<the unit>", () => { … })`.

rules.title: `describe` takes a plain synchronous callback
rules.fix_reason: async work moves into a hook or test, and parameters out of the callback
fix_steps: Move async setup into `beforeAll`.
Drop the callback's parameters and any `return`.

rules.title: `expect` is called right and awaited when async
A promise with assertions is awaited
rules.fix_reason: the test becomes `async` and the chain is awaited or returned
fix_steps: Make the test `async` and `await` the promise, or return it.

rules.title: Test titles are non-empty strings without stray spaces
`toHaveBeenCalledWith` over `toHaveBeenCalled`
rules.fix_reason: the expected arguments are the author's to write
fix_steps: Replace `toHaveBeenCalled()` with `toHaveBeenCalledWith(<the expected arguments>)`.

rules.title: `describe(fn)` for a block about an imported function
`test.each` over a loop of tests
rules.fix_reason: the loop's data becomes a table and its body a parameterised test
fix_steps: Turn the loop's values into a table: `test.each([[1, 2], [3, 4]])`.
Move the loop body into the test callback, with the values as its parameters.

rules.title: A test ends with an assertion
rules.fix_reason: what to assert after the last action is the author's to write
fix_steps: Add an assertion on the effect of the last statement, or move that statement before the last assertion.

rules.title: An equality matcher for an equality
rules.fix_reason: `toBe` compares with `Object.is`, not `===`: `NaN` and `-0` compare differently, so the author confirms the edit

rules.title: Async tests count their assertions
rules.fix_reason: `expect.hasAssertions()` fails a test that passed without asserting; the author may prefer `expect.assertions(n)`

rules.title: `expectTypeOf` for a type check
rules.fix_reason: `expectTypeOf` checks the static type at compile time; the runtime `typeof` check stops running, so the author confirms

rules.title: Hooks in the order they run
rules.fix_reason: reordering hooks moves their statements; the author checks nothing depends on the old order
fix_steps: Move the hook above the hooks that run after it.

rules.title: Hooks before the tests
rules.fix_reason: moving a hook above tests changes nothing at run time but the author places it
fix_steps: Move the hook above the first test of its block.

rules.title: Test titles start in lower case
A hint on each of several snapshots
rules.fix_reason: the hint names what the snapshot shows; the author writes it
fix_steps: Pass a short hint to each snapshot matcher: `toMatchSnapshot("before save")`.

rules.title: `toBe(true)` over `toBeTruthy()`
rules.fix_reason: `toBe(true)` fails for truthy values other than `true` (`1`, `"x"`), so an assertion that passed may now fail

rules.title: `toStrictEqual` over `toEqual`
rules.fix_reason: `toStrictEqual` also checks `undefined` properties, sparse arrays and class types, so an assertion that passed may now fail

rules.title: `toBeFalsy()` over `toBe(false)`
rules.fix_reason: `toBeFalsy` also passes for `0`, `""`, `null` and `undefined`, so the assertion gets looser

rules.title: `toBeTruthy()` over `toBe(true)`
rules.fix_reason: `toBeTruthy` also passes for any truthy value, so the assertion gets looser

rules.title: Setup code in a hook
rules.fix_reason: the code moves into a `beforeAll` or `beforeEach`, chosen by when it must run
fix_steps: Wrap the statement in `beforeAll` (once) or `beforeEach` (per test).

rules.title: Concurrent snapshot tests use their own `expect`
rules.fix_reason: the test takes its context's `expect` as a parameter, which changes the callback's signature
fix_steps: Take `expect` from the context: `test.concurrent("…", async ({ expect }) => { … })`.

rules.title: `vi.fn` with a type parameter
rules.fix_reason: the mocked function's type is the author's to write; a placeholder like `any` would hide the check
fix_steps: Add the function's type: `vi.fn<typeof realFn>()` or `vi.fn<(id: string) => User>()`.

rules.title: Every test sets a timeout
rules.fix_reason: the right timeout depends on what the test does
fix_steps: Pass the timeout in milliseconds as the last argument: `test("…", async () => { … }, 5_000)`.

rules.title: `toThrow` names the error
rules.fix_reason: the expected message or error class is the author's to write
fix_steps: Pass the message, a regular expression or the error class: `toThrow("not found")`, `toThrow(NotFoundError)`.

rules.title: Tests inside a top-level `describe`
rules.fix_reason: wrapping the file's tests in a `describe` needs a title for it
fix_steps: Wrap the file's tests and hooks in `describe("<the unit>", () => { … })`.

rules.title: `data-testid` values follow one pattern
rules.fix_reason: a new test id has to be chosen, and every query that names the old one changes
fix_steps: Rename the test id to the project's pattern, and update every query that names it.

rules.title: No `await` on `fireEvent`
rules.fix_reason: dropping `await` moves the next line a microtask earlier

rules.title: No DOM queries through `container`
rules.fix_reason: the query becomes a Testing Library query by role, label or text, which needs knowing what the user sees
fix_steps: Replace the selector with a query on what the user sees: `screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Save" })`.

rules.title: No `debug()` left in a test
rules.fix_reason: the call only prints; removing it is safe but the author may still be using it

rules.title: Import from your framework's Testing Library
No `g` flag on a regular expression in a query
No manual `cleanup`
rules.fix_reason: the import and the hook both go; the author checks no other teardown hangs on them
fix_steps: Delete the `cleanup` import and the `afterEach(cleanup)` call.

rules.title: No DOM traversal in Testing Library tests
rules.fix_reason: the traversal becomes a query by role, label or text, which needs knowing what the user sees
fix_steps: Replace the traversal with a query: `within(row).getByRole("cell", { name: "Total" })`.

rules.title: No promise passed to `fireEvent`
rules.fix_reason: adding `await` needs the function to be `async`; the author confirms the order

rules.title: No `render` in a setup hook
rules.fix_reason: the render moves into each test, or into a helper the tests call
fix_steps: Move the `render` call into each test, or into a `setup()` helper the tests call.

rules.title: No queries by test id
rules.fix_reason: the query becomes one by role, label or text, which needs knowing what the user sees
fix_steps: Replace it with `getByRole`, `getByLabelText` or `getByText` for what the user sees.

rules.title: No `act` around Testing Library calls
rules.fix_reason: unwrapping the `act` callback moves its statements out, and an `async` one changes shape
fix_steps: Move the statements out of the `act` callback and delete the `act` call.

rules.title: One assertion per `waitFor`
rules.fix_reason: the other assertions move after the `waitFor`, which the author orders
fix_steps: Keep the assertion that waits in the callback; move the others after the `await waitFor(…)`.

rules.title: No side effects inside `waitFor`
rules.fix_reason: the event or render moves before the `waitFor`
fix_steps: Move the event or render before the `await waitFor(…)`.

rules.title: No snapshot inside `waitFor`
rules.fix_reason: the snapshot moves after the `waitFor`, once what it waits for holds
fix_steps: Wait for the condition, then take the snapshot outside the callback.

rules.title: An explicit assertion on a `getBy` query
rules.fix_reason: the matcher the author meant may be another (`toBeVisible`, `toHaveTextContent`)

rules.title: A `getBy` query as its own assertion
rules.fix_reason: the explicit `expect` may assert more than presence; the author confirms

rules.title: `queryBy` in `waitForElementToBeRemoved`
rules.fix_reason: a `queryBy` callback returns `null` where `getBy` threw; the author checks the test still waits for the right thing

rules.title: The query each matcher is meant for
rules.fix_reason: which query pairs with which matcher is the project's configuration
fix_steps: Swap `queryBy…` for `getBy…` (or the reverse) as the project's pairing says.

rules.title: Queries through `screen`
rules.fix_reason: the render result's queries are bound to its container, which `screen` is not when `render` was given another one

rules.title: `userEvent` over `fireEvent`
rules.fix_reason: `userEvent` calls are async and need a `setup()` instance, so the test changes shape
fix_steps: Create `const user = userEvent.setup()` at the start of the test, make it `async`, and replace `fireEvent.click(x)` with `await user.click(x)`.

rules.title: `userEvent.setup()` before user-event calls
rules.fix_reason: the calls move onto an instance created at the start of the test
fix_steps: Add `const user = userEvent.setup()` at the start of the test and call `user.click(…)` and the rest on it.

rules.title: The render result is called `view` or destructured
rules.fix_reason: renaming the variable is local, but the author may prefer to destructure it

rules.title: `describe` takes a plain synchronous callback
rules.fix_reason: async work moves into a hook or test, and parameters out of the callback
fix_steps: Move async setup into `beforeAll`.
Drop the callback's parameters and any `return`.

rules.title: `expect` is called right and awaited when async
A promise with assertions is awaited
rules.fix_reason: the test becomes `async` and the chain is awaited or returned
fix_steps: Make the test `async` and `await` the promise, or return it.

rules.title: Test titles are non-empty strings without stray spaces
No `test.todo` left behind
rules.fix_reason: the missing test has to be written
fix_steps: Write the test, or delete the placeholder.

rules.title: pyproject.toml dependencies are sorted by name
No key or table defined twice in TOML
rules.fix_reason: which of the two definitions was meant can't be known from the file
fix_steps: Decide which definition is right.
Delete the other one, or merge the two tables into one.

rules.title: pyproject.toml declares requires-python
rules.fix_reason: the supported Python range is a project decision; the fix inserts the `python` option, which may not be the right range

python.description: the range the fix writes into `requires-python`

rules.title: pyproject.toml matches its schema
rules.fix_reason: a value the schema rejects is wrong in a way only its author knows how to correct
fix_steps: Read the message: it names the key and the form the schema expects.
Rewrite the value in that form, or move a tool's setting under `[tool.<name>]`.
Run `codelaw check` on the file again until it is clean.

example.dont:
[project]
name = "app"
version = "1.0"
authors = "Ada Lovelace"
dependencies = { requests = ">=2" }
example.do:
[project]
name = "app"
version = "1.0"
authors = [{ name = "Ada Lovelace" }]
dependencies = ["requests>=2"]

rules.title: TOML TODO comments carry a ticket and, when asked, a date
rules.fix_reason: a ticket and a date are facts about the work that only the author knows; the engine can't invent them
rules.dont: # HACK: pinned until the upstream fix
rules.do: # HACK(DEP-3): pinned until the upstream fix
fix_steps: Open or find the ticket for the work and write it in the parentheses: `TODO(ABC-123): …`.
When the project asks for a date (`require_date`), or the work has a deadline, add it: `TODO(ABC-123, 2027-01-31): …`.
For an expired marker: do the work and delete the comment; or, if the work really moves, change the date and say why in the text.
If the comment is not a to-do, rewrite it so it does not open with the tag.

example.dont:
# HACK: pinned until the upstream fix
requests = "2.31.0"
example.do:
# HACK(DEP-3): pinned until the upstream fix
requests = "2.31.0"

rules.title: Overloads of one name sit together
rules.fix_reason: restructure: the overloads have to be moved next to each other, and the order between them is the author's
fix_steps: Move this signature up so that every overload of the name is together, before the implementation.

rules.title: `await` only what can be awaited
rules.fix_reason: removing `await` also removes the pause it makes, which code after it may rely on

rules.title: No @ts-ignore or @ts-nocheck; @ts-expect-error says why
rules.fix_reason: the reason the error is expected has to come from the author
rules.do: // @ts-expect-error: the fixture checks the compiler's message
fix_steps: Fix the type error if you can.
Otherwise replace the comment with `// @ts-expect-error: <why>`.

example.do:
// @ts-expect-error: the fixture checks the compiler's message
const n: number = "1";

rules.title: A literal getter is a readonly field
rules.fix_reason: a field is set on each instance and is visible to `Object.keys`, where the getter lived on the prototype

rules.title: Type arguments on the constructor, not the annotation
Record rather than an index signature
interface for object types
rules.dont: type Point = { x: number; y: number };
rules.do: interface Point { x: number; y: number }

example.dont: type Point = { x: number; y: number };
example.do: interface Point { x: number; y: number }

rules.title: Functions declare their return type
rules.fix_reason: the return type is the author's to write
fix_steps: Add `: ReturnType` after the parameter list.

rules.title: Class members say public, protected or private
Exported functions declare their types
rules.fix_reason: the types are the author's to write
fix_steps: Add `: ReturnType` after the parameter list.

rules.title: Class members are in a set order
rules.fix_reason: moving members carries their comments, and a field's initialiser may read one declared before it, so the order is the author's to change
fix_steps: Move the member up to its group.

rules.title: No Array constructor with several arguments
No non-null assertion next to = or ==
rules.fix_reason: the `!` may have been meant as `!==`; the author decides which
fix_steps: Drop the `!`, or write `!==` if that was meant.

rules.title: No two enum members share a value
rules.fix_reason: which value is right needs the author
fix_steps: Give each member its own value.

rules.title: No delete with a computed key
rules.fix_reason: a `Map` or a rest-destructure changes the data structure
fix_steps: Use a `Map` and its `delete`, or build a new object without the key.

rules.title: No empty interfaces or {} types
rules.fix_reason: the right replacement — `object`, `unknown` or `Record<string, never>` — depends on intent
fix_steps: For any object, use `object`.
For any value, use `unknown`.
For an object with no keys, use `Record<string, never>`.

example.do:
type Options = Record<string, never>;
type Anything = unknown;

rules.title: No explicit any
rules.fix_reason: `unknown` may need narrowing code where the value is used

rules.title: No class used as a namespace
rules.fix_reason: the members become module-level functions, which changes every caller
fix_steps: Export the static members as module-level functions and constants.

rules.title: A Promise is awaited, returned or handled
rules.fix_reason: `void` marks the Promise as deliberately not awaited; awaiting it instead changes when the code after it runs, which only the author can decide

rules.title: A let without a value has a type
rules.fix_reason: the variable's type is the author's to write
fix_steps: Add the type (`let count: number;`) or initialise the variable.

rules.title: An import of only types is import type
No annotation that the value already says
void only as a return type
rules.fix_reason: `undefined` is what `void` means outside a return type; where the author meant a return type, the diff is wrong

rules.title: A namespace is declared once per file
rules.fix_reason: restructure: the two bodies are merged into one, and their order and exports are the author's
fix_steps: Move this body into the first `namespace $N` and delete this one.

example.dont:
namespace Shapes { export const square = 1; }
namespace Shapes { export const circle = 2; }

rules.title: No constructors declared in interfaces, and no `new` methods in classes
rules.fix_reason: the intended constructor signature needs the author
fix_steps: In an interface, describe a constructor with `new (…): T`.
In a class, use `constructor(…)`.

rules.title: No async function where a `void` callback is expected
rules.fix_reason: whether the caller should wait for the work, or the work should handle its own errors, is the author's decision
fix_steps: Use a caller that waits: `for … of` with `await` instead of `forEach`, `await Promise.all(…map(…))` instead of a `forEach` of async work.
Or keep the callback synchronous and handle the Promise inside it: `() => { void work().catch(report); }`.

rules.title: No TypeScript namespaces
rules.fix_reason: moving a namespace's members into a module changes every import
fix_steps: Move the namespace's members to a module of their own.
Export them, and import them where the namespace was used.

rules.title: No ! before ??
rules.fix_reason: removing `!` is right if the left side may be null, which is the point of `??`

rules.title: No non-null assertion after an optional chain
rules.fix_reason: removing `!` widens the type to include `undefined`, which later code may not handle

rules.title: No non-null assertions
rules.fix_reason: handling the null — a check, optional chaining or a default — is the author's choice
fix_steps: Check for null, use optional chaining, or give a default with `??`.

rules.title: No require() calls
rules.fix_reason: an import may need the module's default or named exports chosen by hand
fix_steps: Replace the call with an `import` of the names the code uses.

rules.title: No type the project restricts
rules.fix_reason: the replacement comes from the option's `fixWith`, and another type may not fit every use; a type with no `fixWith` is reported without an edit

types.description: type text → a message, or { message, fixWith }

fix_steps: Use the type the message names.

rules.title: No aliasing this to a variable
rules.fix_reason: the callbacks that use the alias must become arrow functions by hand
fix_steps: Turn the callbacks that use the alias into arrow functions.
Use `this` directly and remove the alias.

rules.title: No assignment a parameter property already makes
rules.fix_reason: removing the assignment is safe only if nothing changes the value in between
fix_steps: Remove the assignment.

rules.title: No extends any or extends unknown on a type parameter
rules.fix_reason: in a .tsx arrow function `<T>` alone parses as JSX and needs `<T,>`

rules.title: No argument typed `any` for a typed parameter
rules.fix_reason: the type the value should have comes from the author
fix_steps: Give the value a type before passing it: annotate it, narrow it, or validate it.
If the parameter really accepts anything, declare it `unknown`.

rules.title: No value typed `any` assigned to a typed target
rules.fix_reason: the type the value should have comes from the author
fix_steps: Give the value a type before assigning it: annotate it, narrow it, or validate it.
If the target really holds anything, declare it `unknown`.

example.do:
const raw: unknown = JSON.parse("8080");
export const port: number = typeof raw === "number" ? raw : 8080;

rules.title: No call of a value typed `any`
rules.fix_reason: the type the value should have comes from the author
fix_steps: Give the value a type: annotate it, or narrow it with a check before the call.
If it comes from an untyped library, add a declaration (`.d.ts`) for it.

example.do:
declare const handler: (n: number) => void;
handler(1);

rules.title: No interface that merges with a class of the same name
rules.fix_reason: whether to rename or to move the members into the class needs the author
fix_steps: Move the interface's members into the class, or rename the interface.

rules.title: No Function type
rules.fix_reason: the right signature needs the author
fix_steps: Write the function's real signature, e.g. `(event: Event) => void`.

rules.title: No member access on a value typed `any`
rules.fix_reason: the type the value should have comes from the author
fix_steps: Give the value a type: annotate it, or narrow it with a check before reading from it.
If it comes from `JSON.parse` or another untyped source, validate it into a typed value first.

example.dont:
declare const config: any;
const port = config.port;
example.do:
declare const config: { port: number };
const port = config.port;

rules.title: No `return` of a value typed `any`
rules.fix_reason: the type the value should have comes from the author
fix_steps: Give the value a type before returning it: annotate it, narrow it, or validate it.
If the function really returns anything, declare its result `unknown` so callers must check it.

rules.title: No expression statements that do nothing
rules.fix_reason: whether a call, an assignment or nothing was meant needs the author
fix_steps: Add the call or assignment that was meant, or remove the statement.

rules.title: Every declared name is used
rules.fix_reason: removing a declaration can drop the side effects of its initialiser
fix_steps: Check the initialiser has no side effect that matters.
Remove the declaration, or use it where it was meant to be used.
For a parameter that must stay for its position, prefix it with `_` and set `argsIgnorePattern: "^_"`.

example.dont:
import { readFile, writeFile } from "node:fs";
export const load = (path: string) => readFile(path);
example.do:
import { readFile } from "node:fs";
export const load = (path: string) => readFile(path);

rules.title: Primitive types, not wrapper object types
No parameter properties
rules.fix_reason: moving the property into the class body adds a field and an assignment
fix_steps: Declare the field in the class and assign it in the constructor.

rules.title: as const instead of repeating a literal as its type
Enum members have initialisers
rules.fix_reason: the suggested value fixes today's order; review it before relying on it

rules.title: A loop that only reads arr[i] is a for-of
rules.fix_reason: value: the loop variable needs a name the code does not contain
fix_steps: Write `for (const item of $A)`, naming the element.
Replace each `$A[$I]` in the body with that name.

rules.title: A function type, not an interface with one call signature
Enum members are literals
rules.fix_reason: the literal value is the author's
fix_steps: Write the value as a literal.

rules.title: namespace, not module, for a TypeScript namespace
A `switch` on a union handles every member
rules.fix_reason: what each missing member should do is the author's decision
fix_steps: Add a `case` for each member of the value's type the `switch` leaves out (hover the value, or read its type, to list them).
If the members left out really share one behaviour, add a `default` instead.

rules.title: No /// <reference path> directives
rules.fix_reason: the matching import needs the module path and what it provides
fix_steps: Replace the directive with an `import` of the module it pointed to.

rules.title: TypeScript's own errors
rules.fix_reason: TypeScript 7.1's API offers no code fixes yet, so each error is fixed by hand
fix_steps: Read the TypeScript error code and message in the finding (`TS2322: …`).
Fix the code, or the type it is checked against, the way `tsc` would ask you to.

rules.title: Names used only as types are imported with type
rules.fix_reason: a type-only import is erased, so code that relied on the module's side effects changes

example.dont:
import { Config, load } from "./config";
export const c: Config = load();
example.do:
import { type Config, load } from "./config";
export const c: Config = load();

rules.title: Overloads that one signature can say are one signature
rules.fix_reason: merging two overloads changes the declared API callers see; the union is offered for an agent or a person to accept
fix_steps: Write one signature with a union type or an optional parameter.

example.do:
function f(x: string | number): void;
function f(x: unknown): void {}

rules.title: GitHub Actions action metadata matches its schema
rules.fix_reason: a misshapen input or run step has several possible meanings; the author picks the one they intended
fix_steps: Read the message: it names the key and what the schema expects.
Add the missing key, or correct the key or the value.
Run `codelaw check` on the file again until it is clean.

example.dont:
name: Setup
description: Set the toolchain up
runs:
  using: composite
  step:
    - run: ./setup.sh
      shell: bash
example.do:
name: Setup
description: Set the toolchain up
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - run: ./setup.sh
      shell: bash

rules.title: GitHub Actions are pinned to a commit SHA
rules.fix_reason: finding the commit a tag points to needs the network, and the engine never uses it (L5)
fix_steps: Look up the commit the tag points to, for example with `git ls-remote https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> <tag>`.
Replace the tag with the 40-character SHA and keep the tag as a comment: `uses: actions/checkout@<sha> # v4.2.2`.
Let Dependabot or Renovate update the pinned SHAs.

example.dont:
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
example.do:
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2

rules.title: GitHub Actions workflows match their schema
rules.fix_reason: a misshapen job or step has several possible meanings; the author picks the one they intended
fix_steps: Read the message: it names the key and what the schema expects, and suggests the key meant when the name is misspelt.
Correct the key or the value.
Run `codelaw check` on the file again until it is clean.

example.dont:
on: push
jobs:
  test:
    runs_on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: npm test
example.do:
on: push
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: npm test

rules.title: No yes/no/on/off as unquoted values
rules.fix_reason: quoting keeps the YAML 1.2 meaning (a string); if a boolean was meant, write `true` or `false` instead

rules.title: No numbers that YAML 1.1 and 1.2 read differently
rules.fix_reason: whether the octal or base-60 meaning or the YAML 1.2 meaning was intended needs the author
fix_steps: For an octal number, write it as `0o755`; for a decimal one, drop the leading zero.
For text such as a port mapping or a time, quote it: `"22:22"`.

rules.title: No key twice in one YAML mapping
rules.fix_reason: which of the two values was meant can't be known from the file
fix_steps: Decide which value the key should have.
Delete the other entry, or give it a key of its own.

example.dont:
service:
  image: nginx
  restart: always
  image: caddy

rules.title: Every alias refers to an anchor defined before it
rules.fix_reason: whether the anchor is missing, misspelt or defined too late needs the author
fix_steps: Find the anchor the alias meant.
Move the anchored node above the alias, fix the spelling, or add the anchor.

rules.title: YAML TODO comments carry a ticket and, when asked, a date
rules.fix_reason: a ticket and a date are facts about the work that only the author knows; the engine can't invent them
fix_steps: Open or find the ticket for the work and write it in the parentheses: `TODO(ABC-123): …`.
When the project asks for a date (`require_date`), or the work has a deadline, add it: `TODO(ABC-123, 2027-01-31): …`.
For an expired marker: do the work and delete the comment; or, if the work really moves, change the date and say why in the text.
If the comment is not a to-do, rewrite it so it does not open with the tag.

example.dont:
# TODO: pin the image digest
image: app:latest
example.do:
# TODO(OPS-18): pin the image digest
image: app:latest

rules.title: No rule pack and no local rule is configured
fix_steps: Run `codelaw init` to install the rule packs for the languages in this repo, or add a rule under `.codelaw/rules/`.

rules.title: File is not valid UTF-8 and was skipped
fix_steps: Re-encode the file as UTF-8, or exclude it in `codelaw.toml`.

rules.title: File is larger than `[files] max_file_size` and was skipped
fix_steps: Exclude the file, or raise `[files] max_file_size` in `codelaw.toml`.

rules.title: File is marked generated and was skipped
fix_steps: Fix the generator instead, or set `[files] lint_generated = true`.

rules.title: A rule failed on this file
fix_steps: Report the rule and file to the rule's maintainer; the rest of the run is unaffected.

rules.title: File is not formatted
fix_steps: Run `codelaw format` (or `codelaw fix`) on the file.

rules.title: The formatter left the file as it was
fix_steps: If the file does not parse, correct the syntax error and run `codelaw format` again.
Otherwise the formatted text failed verification; add the file to `[format] exclude` and report it with the file attached.

rules.title: File changed on disk during the run, so the fix was not written
fix_steps: Run `codelaw fix` again once the file is no longer being edited.

rules.title: The fixed file could not be written, so it is unchanged
fix_steps: Make the file writable (its permissions, a read-only disk, a full disk), then run `codelaw fix` again.

rules.title: A `codelaw-ignore` comment has no reason
fix_steps: Write the reason after a colon: `codelaw-ignore <rule>: <reason>`.

rules.title: A deprecated symbol is used
fix_steps: Replace the use with the replacement `.codelaw/deprecations.toml` names (or the deprecation marker's message gives).
An existing use may stay until its deadline only through `.codelaw/baseline/graph--no-deprecated-usage.toml`, which a person adds with `codelaw baseline add`.

rules.title: A baseline entry allows more findings than its file has
fix_steps: Run `codelaw baseline prune` (or `codelaw fix`, which prunes too) to lower the entry; lowering is always safe.

rules.title: An exception (a baseline entry, a deprecation, a `codelaw-ignore`) expires within its warning window
fix_steps: Fix the findings the exception covers before its `expires` date: on that day they are reported again and the exception is an error.
To keep it longer, a person moves `expires` later with `codelaw baseline add --expires …` (a baseline entry) or edits the comment; `codelaw baseline check` flags an extended deadline for review.

rules.title: An exception reached its `expires` date and no longer covers anything
fix_steps: Fix the findings it covered; they are reported again at their rule's own severity.
Then remove the exception: `codelaw baseline prune` (or `codelaw fix`) lowers a baseline entry, and the `codelaw-ignore` comment is deleted by hand.

rules.title: An exception has no `expires` date while `[exceptions] require_expiry` is on
fix_steps: Add `expires = "YYYY-MM-DD"` (the first day it no longer holds): `codelaw baseline add --expires …` rewrites a baseline entry; a `codelaw-ignore` takes `expires=YYYY-MM-DD` before its colon.

rules.title: An exception's `added_by` is not an email address, or not the git author of the change
fix_steps: Set `added_by` (`by=` in a `codelaw-ignore`) to your own git email, `git config user.email`; `codelaw baseline add` writes it for you.

rules.title: A `codelaw-ignore` comment names a rule that does not exist
fix_steps: Correct the rule id, or remove the comment.

rules.title: A new or edited function is reached by no test file
fix_steps: Write a unit test that imports the function (or its module, for a function the module does not export) and calls it: a test needs judgment, so codelaw does not write one.

If the function should never need its own test (a thin wrapper, generated code), exempt it in `.codelawignore` — `<path>#<name> graph/untested-function forever: <reason>`; to defer the test, give the line `expires=YYYY-MM-DD` and `on_touch=…` and a reason.

rules.title: A new or edited function's line coverage is under `[coverage] min`
fix_steps: Add test cases that run the lines the coverage report shows as missed, regenerate the lcov report in the same job, and run `codelaw check --coverage <report>` again: a test needs judgment, so codelaw does not write one.
If the function cannot reasonably be covered, exempt it in `.codelawignore` — `<path>#<name> graph/function-coverage` with `expires=` or `forever`, `on_touch=` and a reason.

rules.title: The coverage report does not match this file, so its coverage is not judged
fix_steps: Regenerate the lcov report from the code being checked — in the same CI job, after the tests and before `codelaw check` — and pass it with `--coverage` or `[coverage] report`.

rules.title: A `.codelawignore` line matches no file or function
A `.codelawignore` line is missing a field or contradicts itself, so it exempts nothing
fix_steps: Give the line what the message names: the rules it exempts after the target, each a rule this project has or a namespace (`js/*`); a reason after a colon (always, with `expires=` or `forever`); `expires=YYYY-MM-DD` or `forever` (`[codelawignore] require_expiry`); and `on_touch=error|warn|keep` unless it is `forever` (`[codelawignore] require_on_touch`).
`forever` takes no `expires=`, `warn_days=` or `on_touch=`; a glob takes no `on_touch_scope=function`; no line exempts a `codelaw/` rule.

rules.title: A rule is turned `"off"` in the config without a `reason` while `[rules] require_reason` is on
fix_steps: Write the entry as a table with a reason: `"py/no-print" = { severity = "off", reason = "CLI tool: print is the output" }` (SR-CONFIG decision 11c).

rules.title: A commit message does not follow `[commits]` (Conventional Commits by default)
fix_steps: Reword the message to the form the finding shows: `git commit --amend` for the last commit, `git rebase -i <base>` and `reword` for an earlier one; a message is never rewritten for you.
If the convention is wrong for this repository, change `[commits]` in `codelaw.toml` (`preset`, `types`, `scopes`, `subject_max`, `subject_case`, `ticket`, `skip`).

rules.title: The branch name does not follow `[branches]`
fix_steps: Rename the branch (`git branch -m <new-name>`), push it under the new name and open the pull request from it; the finding shows a name that passes.
Or change `[branches] pattern` or `max_length`, or add the branch to `[branches] protected`.

rules.title: The pull request changes more lines than `[pr] max_lines`
fix_steps: Split the change into pull requests that each stand alone — the refactor first, then the feature that uses it.
Lockfiles and generated files are not counted: add other generated paths to `[pr] exclude`, or raise `[pr] max_lines`.

rules.title: The pull request's title or description does not follow `[pr]`
fix_steps: Edit the pull request as the finding says: a title that matches `[pr] title_pattern`, a ticket in the title or description, each section of `[pr] template_sections` filled in.
Then run the CI job again: the description is read from what the CI hands the job, never fetched.
